home: building companies from breakthrough technologies
The journey from scientific discovery to a company that changes an industry is rarely straightforward—and rarely funded.

Over the next decade, the most important companies will emerge from advances in biology, materials, and computation. Yet the system to translate these breakthroughs is broken. Most capital arrives too late, and most institutions are not built to commercialize foundational science.
1955 Capital focuses on this translational gap —investing before markets are obvious and working closely with founders, scientists, and innovators to turn early discoveries into real companies.

Led by Andrew Chung, formerly General Partner at Khosla Ventures and investor at Lightspeed Ventures, the firm was founded in 2016 on the conviction that the defining companies of the next era are being created today—often from science that traditional investors overlook.

We partner from the earliest stages to shape technology, build teams, and accelerate the path from lab to scale. This thesis-driven, operator-led approach has led to top-quartile performance since inception and partnerships with leading global investors.

Transforming how energy and industrial systems are built and operated. We invest across power, infrastructure, and materials—enabling more efficient, scalable, and resilient systems, from next-generation batteries to industrial processes.

Advancing the next generation of biological and health platforms. We focus on diagnostics, therapeutics, and programmable biology—enabling earlier detection, more precise treatments, and entirely new capabilities in human health.

Feeding the world sustainably requires rethinking how food and resources are produced at scale. We invest in foundational technologies—from alternative proteins to agricultural systems and water infrastructure—that enable more resilient global supply chains.
Applying advances in computation to real-world systems. We back AI, robotics, and data-driven platforms that unlock new capabilities across physical and biological domains.

home: Making trust instant, open and programmable
A research-driven global investment firm since 2018
We founded 1kx in 2018 on a structural claim: trust was about to become contestable, and the largest outcomes in technology would accrue to the networks and companies that compressed its cost.

Eight years, three market cycles, and more than 160 investments later, that claim has held. Decentralized finance, stablecoin payments, and the protocols beneath them produced the outcomes our 2018 thesis predicted. The data has sharpened the framework: Cost of Trust 2.0 names the two mechanisms by which the prize is captured.

What hasn't changed is how we work. We underwrite on fundamentals. We commit across cycles. We partner with founders building configurations that compound: the ones that require a blockchain to exist.
Backing the networks and companies that lower the cost of trust.
Cost of Trust 2.0 Flagship thesis, June 2026
Roughly 35% of the US labor market is trust-enabling work: auditors, escrow agents, intermediaries, paperwork.
Blockchain reduces the cost of establishing that trust toward zero.
Cost of Trust 1.0 named the addressable surface. 2.0 names the two mechanisms by which it is captured.

about: Even in the age of instant electronic communication, there is no substitute for face-to-face discussions and informal get-togethers. That’s why we have offices in key biotech hubs in both the US and Europe, so that we can interact more productively with the entrepreneurs we support. These offices also enable us to tap more effectively into the deep talent pools and scientific networks in and around those hubs.
Abingworth has raised 15 funds dedicated to investing in life sciences and healthcare.

Our most recent venture fund, Abingworth Bioventures 8, raised $466 million while Abingworth’s Clinical Co-Development Fund 2 and Clinical Co-Development Co-Investment Fund raised $466 million and $356 million respectively. All are actively investing.
The funds invest in private and public companies across three broad strategic areas: seed and early stage, development stage (including VIPEs and public markets) and clinical co-development.
abingworth.com.desc: We are Abingworth, a trans-atlantic bio-science investment firm with a deep understanding of both the science and markets we invest in.
home: Since our first biotech investment nearly forty years ago, Abingworth has helped young biopharma companies on both sides of the Atlantic turn the latest scientific discoveries into dozens of new treatments for patients.

That process requires time, patience, determination, experience and capital—all of which we provide to our portfolio companies. As the pace of life science research continues to increase, so does the flow of discoveries with the potential to yield new therapeutics. We look forward to working with the next generation of biopharma companies to convert that potential into reality.

1987. That’s when Abingworth made its first investment in a biotech startup. In the decades since, we’ve invested in more than a hundred young companies. Along the way, we’ve helped entrepreneurs navigate through almost every conceivable scenario, good and bad, boom and bust. That’s taught us a lot about building successful companies—experience we love to share with the teams in our portfolio companies.

Innovation is of course the hallmark of the companies in which we invest, but also of Abingworth itself. To prosper as long as we have in the sometimes-precarious world of life-science investing, we have developed our own novel approaches to augment the early-stage investing that has always been at the heart of our strategy.
Examples include our pioneering work with “VIPEs” (Venture Investments in Public Equities) and Clinical Co-Development.
With offices in London, New York and San Francisco we are plugged into new developments—and easily accessible to entrepreneurs—in the key biotech hubs on both sides of the Atlantic.

home: Bookstores, Tea Shops & Museums: Romantic Places for Quiet Souls

In a world that often equates romance with noise, spectacle, and grand gestures, quiet souls crave something else—depth, comfort, and intimacy that doesn’t have to shout to be heard. For those who value reflection over flash and substance over stimulation, the most romantic places are often the simplest: a tucked-away bookstore, a softly lit tea shop, or the still corridors of a museum. These spaces invite a different kind of connection—one that grows in silence, observation, and shared appreciation.
Bookstores: The Romance of Shared Curiosity

There’s something quietly intimate about wandering through a bookstore with someone you’re getting to know. You don’t have to maintain eye contact the entire time, and the natural pauses between shelves give both people a chance to breathe. You can explore side by side, occasionally exchanging a title, a quote, or a memory triggered by a book’s cover. The interaction is low-pressure but meaningful.

Bookstores also reveal a person’s inner world. What they’re drawn to, what they linger on, what they put back without a word—all of it speaks. You learn more about each other through shared silences than you might in an hour of conversation in a loud bar. And when you do speak, the topics are naturally more personal, shaped by ideas and stories rather than surface-level questions.

Ending the outing with a quiet coffee or tea while flipping through your finds only deepens the experience. It’s not just about reading—it’s about showing someone what draws you in and letting them do the same.
Tea Shops: Soft Spaces for Gentle Conversation

Unlike the clatter and chaos of trendy cafés or nightspots, tea shops offer a softer alternative. The lighting is dimmer, the music quieter, and the atmosphere more intentional. Everything slows down in a tea shop—from the way drinks are poured to the way conversations unfold. There’s space to sit close without shouting, to sip slowly, to hold a moment a little longer than usual.

This kind of environment helps sensitive people stay connected to themselves and each other. You’re not overwhelmed by external noise, so you can focus on the small cues—how someone looks at you when you’re speaking, how your energies settle into a shared rhythm. A date here isn’t about making an impression. It’s about offering presence.

Choosing a tea based on mood, sharing a pot instead of ordering separately, or just sitting in companionable quiet all say something meaningful. These small rituals create safety and warmth, which allows vulnerability to emerge naturally—not forced, but welcomed.

Clean Food describes food that is produced in a controlled environment free from microbial contamination, antibiotics, additional growth hormones, pesticides, insecticides or food dyes, using sustainable and resource-efficient production methods. It is the production of agricultural products directly from cell cultures and microorganisms that would have otherwise been derived from conventional farming methods.

This encompasses the utilisation of biotechnology, synthetic biology or tissue engineering, to produce proteins, fats, or tissues. Meat, fish, dairy and leather can already be produced by these means. Agronomics has an established portfolio of venture-stage companies in this exciting and rapidly advancing sector.

home: AI Grant - accelerator for seed-stage AI startups
What type of company or project qualifies?

Anything that leverages AI models in a useful or engaging way. In particular, we're looking for technical & pragmatic founders who want to build great products. If you get a thrill from making something that other people love to use, and you understand that building a new product is 1% idea and 99% iteration, we want to support you. Our focus with AI Grant is on pre-seed/seed-stage startups.

It is an investment. When we started AI Grant in 2017, we handed out much smaller grants for fundamental research. We awarded grants to 36 individuals , who went on to do important research, and to found companies like Cohere , Helia , and Cresta .

Five years later, it seems much has changed: AI research is abundant, but UX and product innovation is just getting started, and so we're relaunching the program with a focus on AI products & investments versus AI papers & grants.
AI Grant is run by Hersh Desai and Lenny Bogdonoff . Nat and Daniel have invested $10M in AI Grant. The company investments themselves are made by AI Grant LLC.
Will you fund multiple projects working on the same thing?

Yes. We plan to fund many companies; some form of overlap is bound to happen. Ultimately, we don't think this will be an issue because we strongly believe the AI product market is enormous -- large enough to support both Lyft and Uber or Bing and Google.

We're looking for smart and energetic people with actionable ideas that are clearly useful. Demos are a big plus; not just because they're fun to look at, but because they hint at the type of person that cares about the end-user experience, which is ultimately all that matters.

No, but you will need one if you're accepted into the program. We only invest in Delaware corporations, but you can create one from almost anywhere in the world with Stripe Atlas (or other programs) in only a few days.

home: AiiM Partners invests in technology companies improving resource efficiency across three interconnected markets - digital transformation, energy & power, and supply chain & logistics - an estimated $17 trillion opportunity. The resource savings our companies create are the delta. The returns those savings compound into are the alpha.

We invest at the commercialization stage, after the technology is proven and as it begins to scale. The companies we back are built on hard, defensible assets, with strong unit economics and traction ahead of their peers. Far fewer funds invest at this stage than at seed or growth, and that scarcity is our advantage: less competition for the best companies, and entry at prices set before the market reaches consensus.

The markets we invest in are among the world's largest and the resource inefficiencies inside them remain vast and unaddressed. We back companies where the waste is greatest and the technology to remove it now exists, companies the market continues to validate: for every $1 AiiM invests, portfolio companies go on to raise $155 in follow-on capital.
We lead or co-lead financings, take active board seats, and put a global network of customers, operators, and strategic partners to work from the day we invest.
AiiM has successfully exited multiple portfolio companies, validating the firm's ability to identify category-defining companies early.

Every investment carries outcome targets set before we commit, and we report results against them. AiiM is the only independent venture fund on BlueMark's Leadership Board and our results are independently verified.The portfolio is on track to offset the equivalent of one gigaton of greenhouse gases and create 5,000 quality jobs, concentrated in low- and middle-income communities.

about: The Alante Team is bound by a shared belief that there is an enormous, emerging opportunity for technology to help the fashion, home and outdoor industries preserve our natural environment and support human rights, while meeting growing and rapidly evolving consumer demand.

Our complementary backgrounds across early-stage investing, financial services, sustainable apparel and supply chain reform, combined with our deep industry connectivity, give us unique insight into selecting and supporting the most promising solutions to the industry’s strategic challenges and commitments at the intersection of sustainability and profitability .
We are diligent and thoughtful investors that back systemic change towards a sustainable future for the ecosystem of the fashion, home and outdoor industries.

Karla brings over 12 years of experience in venture capital and impact investing and another 7 years working in economic development in emerging markets. Prior to Alante, she was Interim Investment Director at VilCap Investments where she led initial investments in early-stage companies in Mexico, Ghana, Kenya, and the US. She supported a large portfolio of companies, cultivated new investor relationships and raised capital for the fund. She also prepared early-stage FinTech and HealthTech entrepreneurs to raise capital through Village Capital’s Mexico-based accelerator program.

Karla has dedicated her career to using business as a force for positive social and environmental impact. Early on she developed a deep passion for reforming production practices across industries to improve working conditions and protect the environment. Her passion for supply chain reform, deep concern with the state of the apparel industry and her love of beautiful clothes, led her to create Alante Capital in an effort to spur innovations that can have lasting positive impacts on people and the planet.
Leslie Harwell, Co-Founder & Managing Partner

Leslie has over 17 years experience in financial services. Prior to Alante, Leslie was Vice President of Sustainable Finance at JPMorgan Chase & Co. where she developed & led the Capital Strategies Initiative for Sustainable Finance in the Americas, and was involved in the management of and value creation in the Social Finance Principal Investing portfolio.
Eileen Fisher has partnered with Alante as an investor and chief advisor. She is the Founder and Chairwoman of EILEEN FISHER, INC.

Karim is a technology veteran with deep experience in product and innovation management and rapid business growth and scaling – particularly in the healthcare and financial services markets. Karim has been an active investor and mentor to a number of technology businesses in Egypt and the US. He is founder and Chairman of D-Kimia Diagnostic Solutions developing fast, affordable, and accurate medical diagnostics using nano-technology and focused on controlling the Hepatitis C epidemic in Egypt and globally.

Karim has served on the board of D-Kimia, Integreight, Shezlong.com, Prognos.ai, and Simplex Arabia CNC Solutions. He is also Chairman of the entrepreneurship committee of the Egyptian National Competitiveness Council, a mentor to high impact entrepreneurs through the Endeavor network, and a fellow of the Aspen Global Leadership Network.

Previously, Karim was SVP, Products and Engineering at WebMD, Inc., directing product management, technology strategy and engineering. Prior to WebMD, Karim was co-founder and CTO of Riskclick, Inc., a software firm specializing in commercial insurance applications. He also was a senior associate at Booz Allen & Hamilton where he was a member of the Global e-Commerce team.
Karim received his PhD in Information Systems from MIT and a dual BSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Carnegie Mellon University.

Tarek Assaad is Managing Partner at Algebra Ventures, Egypt’s leading VC firm. Algebra’s $54M first fund invested in 21 companies including some of Egypt’s most prominent technology startups. Its new $100M fund is actively investing in Egypt and the region.

Prior to Algebra, Tarek was Managing Partner at Ideavelopers where he had been managing $50m of VC investments since 2009 and where he led the fund’s investment in Fawry, the first venture-backed company to go public in Egypt and to become a unicorn.
Tarek started his career as an engineer at Lucent Technologies then as a software developer at SAQQARA Systems, an internet startup in Silicon Valley.

about: âWe founded AlphaDrive with the understanding that the AI revolution is not just a technological shift,â Yaron says, âbut a fundamental change in how companies build products, design business models, and compete.â And if thatâs true, then the role of a fund has to change with it.
We founded AlphaDrive with the understanding that the AI revolution is not just a technological shift, but a fundamental change in how companies build products, design business models, and compete.

In our approach to working with founders, it is not enough to identify a meaningful market need, it is equally critical to ensure real demand exists. home: Our fund invests alongside 100+ expert angels. One line on your cap table that brings founders expertise and network.
You get the best of both: hands-on angels to move fast, and a €22M fund that’s got your back.
We’re the first believers in your story, often leading your pre-seed round with the first cheque in
We activate our angel network for intros, advice, sparring and our tailored leadership program: Arches Academy.
You deserve clarity. That’s why we share our terms and processes from day one. So you know exactly where you stand.
We back ambition and stay for the journey.
We invest in Benelux based B2B software startups, typically at the pre-seed stage with ticket sizes between €250K and €1M.

To respect both your time and ours, we start with a short video call. If there’s a fit, we schedule a second meeting with another team member to ensure a balanced view. We might ask for extra details and will always share honest, constructive feedback.

The next step in our process is the Monthly Meeting with our angels. Each month, we host one in-person and one online session where selected startups pitch to our network of Archangels. After your pitch, you’ll have the chance to join informal, face-to-face discussions with investors, where you can validate your business case and receive honest feedback.

We’re fully transparent, our term sheet is available from the start. At Arches, we believe in fair terms. We use standardised documents, trusted by follow-on investors, that keep legal costs low. For many founders, this is the first time dealing with these documents. That’s why we’ve added clear and simple explanations to our term sheet.

about: Sir Richard Branson’s Virgin Group that stands for entrepreneurship, sustainability and growth working in unison to achieve corporate goals, inspired Anirudh A Damani to create Artha Group. He chose early stage investing and renewable energy as the focus areas for the group. In renewable energy, Anirudh sees the ability for each village of India to become a centre of economic growth and in Indian entrepreneurship the thrust to light up our great country.

He overlooks all the activity of the group and is primarily responsible for maintaining and promoting the corporate culture and ethics and is the group’s spokesperson. Recently, he has taken on the responsibility of GP for the first early stage VC fund out of the Artha stable.

Animesh has always been inclined towards entrepreneurship. A graduate from Babson College, Massachusetts, he began his career with an internship at Mumbai Angels which helped him gain insight into the Indian venture capital industry. With the help of his family office, AIV, he gained a first-hand perspective on the whole sector.

In 2012, Animesh’s family took over the struggling hospitality business of Platinum Hotels in Ahmedabad. He stepped up to the challenge and successfully turned around the operations, making the hotel brand profitable.

The very next year Artha decided to expand and set up Artha Energy Resources (AER), India’s first and only investment bank focused on the Indian renewable energy sector, which has advised on renewable energy transactions worth $812 million. With the help of his team, Animesh has set-up a data-driven business that maps 99% of renewable capacity and 40% of power consumers in India.

about: I started Atelier to fund a specific vision of the world: a world in which people are able to do what they love for a living and to have a more fulfilling and purposeful life.

As an immigrant to the US, I’ve always been captivated by the notion of the American dream and how to broaden access. The Passion Economy thesis is the distillation of that idea: that technology platforms can build a better world, advance economic opportunity, and lower the barriers to entrepreneurship.

I’ve always been a creator: I studied art intensively between age 5 and 18 and have been writing prolifically my entire life. I have immense respect for people who create something from nothing and who make their passion their life’s work.

I fell in love with the divine discontent of founders while investing at Andreessen Horowitz. The act of starting something is to make a statement that we are not, and should not be, content with the way that things are in the world. Founders challenge the status quo by starting a company. As an investor, I have the privilege of supporting them along the way in realizing their visions.
Atelier wouldn’t exist without the support of our investors, mentors, and founders who have believed in me since day 1—for them, I am immensely grateful.

Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) 컴퓨터공학 학/석사, UC Berkeley Haas MBA

맹두진 대표는 2002년 투자업을 시작하여 AI, 반도체, 로보틱스, 모빌리티 등 딥테크 산업을 중심으로 서비스 및 소프트웨어 분야에 이르기까지 폭넓은 투자를 진행해 왔으며, 다수의 포트폴리오 기업 IPO 경험을 보유하고 있습니다. 기술 경쟁력을 기반으로 글로벌 시장을 선도할 수 있는 기업에 주목하며, 에이티넘인베스트먼트 합류 전에는 삼성전자 종합기술원에서 연구원으로 근무하였습니다. 또한 2011년에는 한국벤처캐피탈협회(KVCA) 선정 최우수 심사역으로 선정된 바 있습니다.
[휴머노이드 & 로봇] 홀리데이로보틱스, 디든로보틱스, Apptronik, 메디인테크, 클로봇 [반도체] 오픈엣지테크놀로지, 보스반도체, 비씨엔씨 [Physical AI] 다임리서치, 원프레딕트 [모빌리티] 라이드플럭스, 모빌테크 [AI서비스 & SW] 이팝소프트, 그렙, TanTan, 원티드랩
2005년 에이티넘인베스트먼트에 합류한 황창석 사장은, 존슨앤존슨메디칼을 거쳐 한림창업투자에서 바이오/헬스케어 분야 투자 경험을 축적해왔습니다. 현재 에이티넘인베스트먼트의 주요 펀드의 대표펀드매니저를 맡고 있으며, 2006년 산업자원부장관상을 수상한 바 있습니다.

김제욱 부사장은 2010년 에이티넘인베스트먼트에 합류하여 AI, 서비스, 엔터프라이즈 소프트웨어 등 IT 분야 투자를 중심으로, 컨슈머까지 폭넓은 투자를 주도하고 있습니다. IT 기술을 통해 기존 시장을 혁신하는 스타트업에 주목해 왔으며, 에이티넘인베스트먼트 합류 전 삼성전자 SW연구소에서 소프트웨어 개발 및 기술전략 업무를 수행하였습니다. 2016년 한국벤처투자(KVIC) 우수심사역, 2021년 한국벤처캐피탈협회(KVCA) 최우수심사역에 선정되었으며, 2023년에는 중소벤처기업부 장관 표창(KVCA)을 수상한 바 있습니다.

home: Empowering The Next Wave Of Life Science Innovation
We are a leading San Diego biotech venture fund focused on first-in-class innovations to transform patient care.

For over 40 years, Avalon BioVentures has been driving life sciences innovation by investing in and building pioneering biotech companies that address critical unmet medical needs. We don’t just fund companies—we create them. Our team of seasoned entrepreneurs and operators work side-by-side with visionary founders, providing the capital, expertise, mentorship, and infrastructure needed to translate cutting-edge science into breakthrough therapies for patients in need.

We invest in innovative science at the earliest stages, seeking out white space opportunities that are often too early for other investors. We like to be first and do not shy away from scientific risk. From company formation to successful exits, our hands-on approach ensures that each of our companies has the strategic guidance and operational support needed to thrive.

Through our ABV Accelerator, we provide portfolio companies with immediate access to world-class scientific, operational, and financial resources. This fully integrated model expedites development timelines and optimizes capital efficiency, with the goal of rapidly developing potentially life-changing innovations for patients who need them most.

Avalon BioVentures has a long and successful track record of investing in and building life science companies. Our strategy is rooted in identifying and developing disruptive technologies, working closely with world-class scientists, academic institutions, and industry leaders to uncover and translate cutting-edge research into high-impact businesses with the ultimate goal of improving patient outcomes.

Dr. Behzad Aghazadeh, PhD is the Managing Partner and Portfolio Manager of Avoro Capital. He has over 25 years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry spanning scientific research, management consulting, institutional investing, and board leadership.

Behzad received his master’s degree in Physics from the Ludwig-Maximilians-University and a PhD from Cornell University in Biochemistry & Biophysics. He continues to serve on the boards of public and private biotechnology companies.

about: At SV8, we embed acquisition thinking into the DNA of our portfolio companies from inception. This strategic approach creates exceptional value for both founders and investors.
As M&A experts note: "Positioning yourself now for the M&A wave that will likely arrive in the next couple of years means seeing your startup through the eyes of a potential acquirer."

The harsh reality is that most startups will exit through acquisition rather than IPO. We help founders develop business models, product roadmaps, and go-to-market strategies with potential acquirers in mind.
Our deep M&A expertise enables us to anticipate how strategic buyers evaluate acquisition targets — guiding critical decisions from day one.

The M&A process is complex, fast-paced, and emotionally challenging. According to industry experts, "Psychologically, you should prepare yourself for some sort of turmoil. You are operating in a different environment now where your ownership and drive and hustle will likely change."
We help founders navigate the identity shift that comes with exit planning, addressing the psychological barriers that often diminish exit value.
Leading entrepreneurs understand that "psychological preparation can be used to facilitate sensemaking and negotiation" during the acquisition process.

We help founders identify the most likely acquirers years before an exit, guiding strategic decisions that maximize acquisition appeal and building relationships with potential acquirers well in advance of any transaction discussions.

about: Baseline is an independent community and workspace for early-stage founders who are building breakout and break-through tech companies in Ireland. It's a space where founders can experiment, build velocity, and be plugged into a global network of like-minded founders. We believe that:

As a community of technical, creative, and commercial founders, we share the highs and lows of early stage startup building together. We have high expectations of ourselves, and each other. If someone needs help, we step in and lend a hand, and we should expect the same in return.

Baseline is not operated as a programme, and does not provide mentors. We are not a shared office space, and we don't offer dedicated desks. Our members are self-directed, and value being part of a peer group of like-minded founders, executing with urgency.

We are a community first, workspace second. Baseline is located in the heart of Dublin's Liberties. Our space is comfortable, spacious and designed to be flexible for getting focused or team work done in a mix of open areas and private meeting rooms.

The space is fully air conditioned, with three aspects of daylight, a full kitchen, bike storage, and accessible facilities, including WC's & shower rooms. We're a 24/7, always-on community, and so is the workspace. Members are able to come and go as they please, bring guests, and use the space to host their own events.

Baseline is founded by Fiona Kelly and Eamon Leonard, former founders and angel investors. Fiona works closely with founders on finance, operations, and fundraising. She has built a career on making complex systems feel simple [ LinkedIn ]. Eamon helps founders with product development, go-to-market, and fundraising. He has been building products, leading teams, and creating communities over the past 25 years [ LinkedIn ].

In the interest of both parties, we are transparent on what we want and let you decide if there is a likely match. If our investment focus doesnât blend with your business model or capital strategy, that means we are simply not meant for each other.

We are passionate about disruptive technologies and the business opportunities that these create. We are looking for innovation pioneers challenging the status quo in traditional sectors, or dramatically improving legacy processes. The companies we fund must have some type of key science or technological innovation leading to the establishment of intellectual property rights.

We invest in enterprise software that is AI-driven, spanning Applied AI & Analytics, customer relationship management (CRM), enterprise resource planning (ERP), and supply chain, with opportunistic investments in cybersecurity and fintech. We also invest in digital-native consumer platforms across sports, wellness, gaming, and entertainment.
We invest primarily in Canadian and US companies. We occasionally invest in companies based in Europe or Israel but those companies must meet an even higher bar.

Traction, growth curve, and unit economics are the most important factors we use to determine specific valuations. Premium valuations would need to be justified with exceptional metrics and technology.

We donât act as lead investor in the first round. We will take a minority position in the first initial round. We will always ask for pro-rata rights to potentially invest in future rounds at larger amounts.
We have a very strong bias towards companies with low cash burns. We also prefer a funding round where our participation usually yields at least 18 months of runway.
Participation in smaller rounds requires companies to have highly disruptive technologies with truly exceptional progress.
We usually require at least two full time founders, with one being technical. We have a strong bias towards startups having strong advisors with shares backing them.

about: Our story started in 2008 when each of us was leading our own business through growth and change. We had sought the wisdom and experience of others and found value in the collective experience and knowledge of three. For different reasons we each sold our businesses to globally-operating and listed entities. Beachhead was formed soon after as our vehicle to pursue what we love – good business ideas backed by passionate and energetic owners.

The three of us bring our own perspectives to each opportunity but we will continue to value our collective judgement rather than a formula. For us to invest, all three must agree. Unlike venture capital funds we use our own capital. This gives us the flexibility to consider each opportunity on its merits rather than imposing artificial benchmarks.

After working in senior roles with global companies in the logistics sector Aaron formed NTS in 2005. It soon found a niche market and grew organically over an 8-year period to a $20m+ business. Now a significant national enterprise, Aaron sold the business to a listed Australian company in 2013.
He continues to operate and consult in the private sector and has driven large changes in corporates that have delivered significant and lasting results for all stakeholders.

Originally an accountant, Aaron understands the importance of keeping a close watch on the financials and has seen many good business falter or fail by placing too much focus on the wrong aspects. He believes it is imperative that all stakeholders in a business are kept firmly accountable and share in the success of a business.
Aaron’s key strengths are operational analysis and continuous improvement. He uses intuition and solid financial skills to get to the heart of any business.
Alan is passionate about technology, innovation and change as it applies to any facet of life. He enjoys business, inspiring and transforming teams.
He is a successful entrepreneur in the technology services sector with a deep understanding of technology trends and markets having built and exited several technology businesses.

home: Beachhead is a venture capital firm investing in high-growth Australian companies looking to rapidly expand, go further and achieve more.
We are an early stage venture capital firm backing exceptional Australian entrepreneurs. We help you with capital, guidance and strategy.
The value we bring is our willingness to take on risk and guide you through the fast-changing environment of growth. Ideally this would prepare you for Series A capital raise or an exit.

Our strengths come from hands-on experience in starting, growing and exiting businesses across a number of industries. We understand the effort and risk you are taking, and offer more than being a silent partner on the sidelines. We prefer to invest in businesses that offer a unique advantage to outcompete established rivals. We are agnostic to industry sector with a focus on scalable unit economics.
There is nothing that drives us more than success – your success.
“ I have a knack for spotting an opportunity that others miss . ”
“ I love the power of smart ideas and good people creating seriously good businesses. ”
“Building something from nothing and challenging the status quo have always been my passion. ”
We seek early stage businesses with the passion and ideas to go all the way. We are looking for people with self-belief, perseverance and some rat cunning.

If it is only money you need, we're probably not the right partner for you. We are looking for early-stage businesses that are looking for both money and where we have an edge to develop their business into something of much greater value. The majority of our investments will be in the $200k- to $1m range where the business already has a product, team and, most importantly, customers.

about: If Alex was asked why did you choose the profession of a venture investor? He would answer: What else could I do? Sometimes you have to stop thinking so much and go where your heart takes you. We believe that Alex’s heart is somewhere between AI and Software, albeit his soul and body actively approaching FoodTech. :o:

Alex is not able to sit still and wait for new opportunities, but proactively creates them. For 15 years in private equity and venture capital investments, he took part in more than 50 transactions with a total volume of over $3.5 billion. Alex's strengths include: structuring deals, finding new opportunities, finance, strategy and sales.

To charm Alex, the project needs strong and unique leaders, tested and digitized hypotheses, and a vision of the team on a long horizon (Alex's planning horizon is rumored to be the longest in history). Unlike most VCs, Alex loves to read long letters and study detailed decks from the founders.
Alex is passionate about Begin and our portfolio 24/7, except when his favorite football team is playing. But we are very lucky that they lose all the time and have few matches per year.

Before dedicating his life to venture capital Ruslan tried himself in all other roles: startup founder, corporate and strategy consultant. Now, two facts he knows for sure: “VC is the best job in the world” and “being a startup founder is awesome, but freaking hard!”

To make founders’ life somewhat easier Ruslan is always happy to share his experience. From building sales teams in US and China to raising $50m+ investment rounds. Prior to Begin Ruslan spent 5 years with Runa Capital where he worked with awesome startups like Mambu, NGINX, and Brainly.

Ruslan is passionate about partnering with entrepreneurs who are focused on building product-driven companies and share Ruslan’s love of excel. You can melt his heart with deep industry knowledge and 5-years product plan.

If you can’t reach out to Ruslan, it is probably because he got lost while exploring jungles in India or national parks in Africa. He also used to sail the ocean and freeride in mountains, but his skills were so poor that his wife wisely banned all life threatening activities.

home: A VC fund is very similar to a TV series. Each investment is a new episode in which founders are actors and investment managers are the casting directors. If the series is successful then there will be a season two.
Alex and Ruslan are sceptical about horror and drama in the investment portfolio, but always looking for a next blockbuster. Reach out to them if you are shooting one.

The first investment season for Begin Capital started in 2020. We invested in 28 blockbusters across all industries and genres. We have led and participate in Seed and Series A rounds with checks from $500k up to $7M. There are no geographic borders for a real hit, but the European market is close to our heart.

The second season of Begin Capital will be dedicated to the world of DeepTech, Artificial Intelligence and the Physical World. Our investment thesis equally values both – mind-blowing technology backend as well as proven industry applications. We'll support the most innovative and ambitious teams from the early days to help them reach singularity :o: With strong advisors on board and love of science fiction, the second casting is open for new applications
We have a global mandate and invest at Pre-seed to Series A stage. Our ticket size is flexible, ranging from $500K to $8M

People are behind every revolution. And we are looking for exceptional founders who are Pirates, Winners and Robots. Pirates . We are looking for founders who are not afraid to make a mistake and always ready to challenge the rules. We call them “Pirates”. Winners . Small goals are not for us. Founders who work with us, always want to conquer the world. Nothing less. We call them “Winners”. Robots . Building a business is hard. Founders shall have a clear understanding of all business processes and be rigorously improving every KPI. Day after day. We call them “Robots”.

Unique ideas are capable of disrupting markets. But we prefer to treat all ideas as hypotheses. And we only invest in hypotheses that are tested and translatable into numbers. Numbers help us make informative and responsible investment decisions. We also believe that no unicorn was built without great attention to the numbers (except for Theranos) :o::o::o:

“Partner” is not just a title for us. In good times and bad, we put the startup’s interests above our own. We' re proud to be partners with founders and encourage close communication with our portfolio.
We're building a new VC fund and consider ourselves entrepreneurs. We want Begin Capital to be the #1 choice for founders and are excited about the work we do every day.
We see our mission is sharing knowledge and experience with our portfolio companies. And if our expertise is not enough, we will find the best experts to help.

about: Behold Venture is a specialist operated fund. All of us on the investment team have spend our careers dedicated to the games industry, making and publishing games, starting new companies, leading and growing existing ones.

We’ve worked on AAA franchises with several hundreds devs, and we’ve helped indie games go to market. In this wide range of experiences there’s one common, red thread through all our journeys - and it’s not only our love for interactive entertainment - but our true interest in the people actually making the games!

Karl Magnus, or KM as most in the Nordics call him, is a game developer and studio leader turned investor. After two decades of building and leading award-winning AAA teams and managing global groups of game studios at companies like DICE and EA , he switched to early-stage investments in 2016. As a private investor he invested in 18 different start-ups before starting Behold Ventures.

Sigurlína, also known as Lina, is an Icelandic engineer and game producer, who after a 15-year stint spanning five cities in four countries in leadership roles on franchises like EVE Online, The Division, Star Wars Battlefront and FIFA has shifted her focus to Behold and investing in early-stage companies.

Magnus has a background as a strategy consultant and corporate finance professional. The last 10 years was spent as the founding partner of Sequent Invest (small cap private equity). Magnus also co-founded several start-ups and has served on the board of numeral companies, most relevant Fast Track Capital and Mionix. In addition, Magnus has made some 20+ business angel investment.

Brynjólfur, commonly known as Binni, is an Icelandic computer scientist and experienced analytics and research leader with 15 years of experience in the game industry. He has played a key role in initiating and leading analytics and research for game franchises such as Minecraft, Toca Boca, Battlefield, EVE Online, The Hunter: Call Of The Wild and Crusader Kings, among many others.

Ali Farha is a senior producer and tech leader with 10+ years of experience. He played a key role in porting Star Stable Online to multiple platforms and is an active voice in the games industry ecosystem.
“We’Ve put together a world-class group of endemic Experts AND ADVISORS, creatING an unparalleled opportunity for our portfolio companies to evolve and grow.”
behold.vc.desc: Behold Ventures is a venture capital fund supporting early-stage video game startups led by passionate entrepreneurs shaping the future of interactive entertainment.
home: Behold Ventures is a venture capital fund, laser-focused on enabling the next generation of game entrepreneurs by calling upon the experiences of the current one. Lifelong commitments to the games industry - as developers, publishers, studio leaders and investors – are now ready to stand by and support new endeavors.

The generations of today favor video games over all other forms of media. Almost half of the entire population of earth play video games and have an active relationship with this form of interactive entertainment - and we’re just getting started.

At Behold, we strongly believe that video games truly are the medium of our century. They are changing how we communicate, interact and relate for the better. Seeing this bright future is a big reason why we invest in video games.

We’re big on people. Behind every idea, vision and daring new venture we always find passionate individuals who in some way want to achieve greatness, fulfill dreams or make a change. The core of these people is of mighty importance to us, and we keep looking for sound values and a true north which aligns much with our own.

In the same way, as we and other investors grill the entrepreneurs on every single detail of their plan, we always encourage them to do the reverse due diligence and pressure test anyone they consider letting onto their cap table. Early-stage investments are much more than cold transactions, it’s like setting out on a long journey together - and the travel company needs to be picked wisely.
“VIDEO GAMES TRULY ARE THE MEDIUM OF THE 20th CENTURY, AND THEY ARE EVOLVING HOW WE INTERACT AS A SPECIES.”

At Behold Ventures, we invest in early-stage video game start-ups founded by ambitious and creative founders with an aptitude for strategic thinking. We look for teams that are hellbent on creating the most amazing entertainment experiences of tomorrow.
We then make it our mission to support, further inspire and multiply the star potential in all of them.

Our goal is to have deep trust relationships with our entrepreneurs, invest early and double down on the company throughout its journey. Web 3 economies, open protocols and DAO’s are built for global audience and user owned through tokens that align incentives. These new companies unlock massive TAMs by eliminating take rates inherent in centralized platforms.

Benson Oak bought AVG in 2004 when it was a 20 person team in Brno, Czech Republic and became actively involved in assisting the management of the Company. At the time, AVG had $5M in revenue but had just started to offer its anti-virus product for free.

Benson Oak became involved in the operations and especially in developing the freemium model as the company grew to over 100 million users, becoming a global leader in Internet Security solutions for consumers and small businesses. In 2005, Enterprise Investors and Intel Capital bought into AVG in a secondary transaction and in 2009, TA Associates entered. Overall, BOCs investment in AVG returned 100x to its investors as the company exceeded a $1 billion market cap after going public on the NYSE in February 2012.

Robert Cohen spearheaded BOC’s acquisition of AVG and was deeply involved in the business for the next 8 years. Aside from being a Board member, Robert also served as interim CFO, managed AVG’s fund raising activities.

In 2011, he joined the senior management team responsible for global M&A and strategic corporate development activity and gained deep operational experience via the execution and integration of five acquisitions and two strategic partnerships, in the US, Germany and Israel. Robert was part of the management team as it went public.
Including Harri (NY), LoungeBuddy (SF, Series A led by Founders Fund), Shoppad (Bay Area, the #1 application developer for Shopify) and co-investments from LP relationships.

学を主席且つ飛び級で卒業し、AIやITの知識技術を極めるために大学院に入学。 大学院卒業後は、大手通信会社のCEO室で自社の成長戦略のためのデータ分析および戦略を担当。 その後、外資系コンサルファームにてAIやWeb3関連の事業戦略立案を担当し、独立。 フリーランスとして様々な企業のWebアプリ開発およびシステム実装/要件整理における幅広いITコンサルを担当。 2023年経産省の高度IT人材として石川県加賀市の企業のDX化を推進。

about: We built and exited technology companies before managing capital. That experience shapes every investment decision we make.
BlackSheep was built on a simple premise: the best investors in technology companies are those who have built them.

Our team has founded, scaled, and successfully exited multiple companies across different markets and economic cycles. We understand the operational reality of building a technology company — from the uncertainty of the early days to the complexity of scaling globally. That experience informs every investment decision we make and every board seat we hold.

BlackSheep was therefore not designed as a purely financial investor. It was designed as an entrepreneurial venture platform — managed through BlackSheep SGR S.p.A. , an AIFM authorized by the Bank of Italy.

BlackSheep is built by entrepreneurs for entrepreneurs. The partners have spent decades operating companies, managing teams, negotiating exits, and navigating growth and crisis alike. This shapes how the firm invests: not through financial engineering alone, but by helping companies build durable businesses. For founders, this means working with investors who understand product-market fit, hiring inflection points, and the psychological realities of company building.

BlackSheep approaches venture capital as a continuation of entrepreneurship — not a purely financial activity. The role of the firm extends beyond capital allocation: it is to help companies become structurally stronger organizations, supporting founders on strategic decisions, go-to-market execution, and organizational scaling. Board participation is active and operational. Capital is only one component of the value created.

BlackSheep follows a revenue-first philosophy. In markets dominated by narrative cycles and valuation inflation, the firm prioritizes companies where real adoption, paying customers, and scalable revenue models already exist. This discipline reduces technological risk and aligns incentives around sustainable growth. The objective is not to chase trends, but to back businesses capable of generating long-term enterprise value.

BlackSheep focuses on industry-specific applications of artificial intelligence and data technologies. Rather than investing in horizontal tools with broad but shallow adoption, the firm concentrates on sectors where AI transforms core economic processes. In these environments, technology is not a feature layer — it becomes a structural component of the operating model. This specialization allows the firm to develop domain knowledge, stronger networks, and better pattern recognition across investments.

Our investment philosophy is rooted in Black Swan Theory (Taleb, 2007) and our screening strategy rests on our development of a unique Black Swan Rating System. Our Black Swan Rating system describes the objective dynamics of potential Black Swans â the mega game-changers of IT and technology â and guides our investment selection.
In Nassim Talebâs 2007 book, âThe Black Swan: The Impact of the Highly Improbableâ, Black Swan is the term Taleb gives to a highly improbable event with three main attributes:

The most notable and largest Black Swan events of recent times in technology, include revolutionisers such as Apple and Facebook, and more recently start-ups like Uber, Airbnb, Tesla and Klarna, that seemingly came out of the blue and went onto turn whole industries upside down. Few people saw them coming, and even those who were told in detail found it difficult to believe â with some of the most experienced and well-heeled Silicon Valley VCs rejecting opportunities when pitched by the hopeful founders.

This is because potential Black Swans are notoriously, and by definition, very difficult to spot before the fact. One reason for this is that revolutionary ideas almost exclusively present with so many unknowns â both known and unknown â and such a huge level of risk, that the classic human response â even for risk-ready enthusiastic VC partners â is to reject the risk and refuse to believe in the opportunity.

Using our unique objective Black Swan Rating System, we aim to identify future Black Swans in IT and technology. We will then give ongoing support to entrepreneurs, providing capital, mentoring and introductions throughout the last phase of the company before IPO, building an extreme impact portfolio, and growing the businesses and networks of all those within it.

Automation technologies allow scarce resources to go further; allowing outputs to grow or stabilise whilst reducing inputs.

about: Javier Ulecia and Miguel del Cañizo have known each other since 1990 when they started working together at Renault in France just after they finished their engineering degrees.

Ten years afterwards, Javier and Miguel collaborated in the launching, management and posterior closing of an Internet Incubator named Doing, focused on broadband products and services (May 2000-March 2001).

After closing Doing, and around the middle of 2001, they started, with the strategic and financial support of Bruno Entrecanales, a new fund (Bullnet Capital I), with the aim of eventually becoming one of the reference players in the incipient Spanish technology VC market.
At that moment, given the very little interest of the investment community in technological projects, we decided to swim against the current and establish our fund on several, basic arguments:

Helped to a great extent by the initial support of Bruno Entrecanales, financial sponsor of the Project, we managed to convince a series of private investors as well as an institutional investor, the European Investment Fund, to, at last, put together in March, 2003 an initial fund of 18 million euros to support the launch of technological start-ups in Spain. Our initial objective was to invest over the following five years in five or six companies around 2 million euros in each one.
Since going into action, Bullnet Capital I invested in five technological companies, all in very early stages of development when investment was made.

During these years the only full time employees were Javier and Miguel, counting on Carmen Arenzana for all the administrative tasks. At that time Carmen was Financial Director of Bruno Entrecanales’ investment company.

In 2007 we started to think of a new fund, Bullnet Capital II, and we concluded that we needed to strengthen the structure of the team. Carmen started to spend more and more time at Bullnet until she became a full time dedicated member in 2009, when the fund rising had just finished. With a short period of time thereafter, we started the recruiting process of a new investment professional resulting in José Luis Gómez joining the team in December 2009.

byFounders was built by a collective of founders who want to help the next generation of ambitious founders emerging from the New Nordics.

Invite us on board as your first investor, and we will be your trusted ally. This is when we can add the most value, and it's something we've done many times before with companies like Lovable, Verda, Sumary, Safetywing, Bob W, Parahelp, Corti, and many, many more. We will encourage, challenge, push, open doors, and serve as your sounding board. Day and night.

What that looks like day-to-day depends entirely on you. Our job is to support, not to control you. There's no set playbook, because no two founders need the same thing — but we'll always go above and beyond for you. Whatever you need, whenever you need it. That could be cold-DMing a candidate to close a hire. Sitting in as chief of staff for six months. Testing the product and telling you what's broken. Tearing apart your deck for the next funding round. Or staying out of the way, when that's your ask.

As a generalist tech fund, we don't hold a sector thesis. We go where the talent is, and we invest in people before ideas. What we're after is the history and the drive that explain why you keep going when things get tough. That's why we'd rather spend time on the hardest things you've been through than overanalyzing market sizing.

Being early also means being genuinely on the same side, so we don't stack the term sheet in our favor with a bunch of protective clauses. We sit in the same share class as you, so there's no version of the outcome where our interests and yours point in different directions. Our full term sheet is public, and we encourage you to read it to understand our approach.
Remember, it's never too early to start a conversation with us — though it can definitely be too late. Reach out, and let's start building our relationship.
Occasionally, when it makes sense. If another investor's competencies and network complement ours, we're glad to bring them along.
It depends, but our process typically runs 2–4 weeks.

We use our 8T framework. It structures how we think about your company and the opportunity it represents. It isn't a checklist you need to tick off, but we encourage you to consider how you'd address each T. Read more

These days, you can do just about anything online—even visit your doctor. So why do you still need to drive across town just to get someone to notarize a document?

That compelling question spurred co-founders Pat Kinsel and Adam Pase to launch Notarize, a firm that—with the help of Camber Creek—is bringing online document verification to some of the largest companies in the world.
Through Notarize, consumers and businesses can connect with an online notary public 24-7 using a computer, tablet, or smartphone.
Of course, achieving scale meant Notarize needed to work with major businesses and other digital products. That’s why Camber Creek:

“Camber Creek has been an amazing partner for us,” Pat says. “From their presence on our board to helping us land major partnerships with leading real estate groups and corporations like Adobe, they’ve been tremendous.”

Now known as Proof, notarization is one of the solutions the company offers. Proof is adding layers of trust to online transactions with products that use a combination of human and digital verification to give all parties assurance. Their software provides an effective counter against the range of tools available to falsify financial records, income, and even identity.

医療・介護業界が抱える 5 つの課題 日本の社会保障費が高止まりする中、医療・介護業界には 5 つの課題が存在するとユカリアは考えています。その課題の根底には、医師を頂点とするヒエラルキー構造が存在します。
ユカリアは、医療・介護業界の課題解決のために、「 5 つの変革テーマ」を設定しています。硬直化した組織・文化を打破し、医療業界を「フラットな構造」に変化させることで、ヘルスケア業界にイノベーションを起こします。
患者起点の思考や商流に至りづらい。また、 製薬企業のような「川上プレイヤー」に利益が偏重し、現場へ還元されない。
患者への付加価値を追及し、医療の質を向上。医療の質向上に尽力する病院が正当に評価される産業へ。
地域包括ケアシステムを構築し、地域で最後まで高齢者を支えぬくことのできる環境を整備。
現場の IT リテラシー不足に加え、現場で必要とされるサービスを開発できる会社も不足。
デジタル化の促進により、医療従事者の就業体験、患者の受診体験の革新的向上を実現。

home: ユカリアの医療経営総合支援事業は、提携医療法人の経営・運営を包括的に支援する「病院経営サポート」を主軸とする一方で、それ以外の病院には様々な「コンサルティング」を提供しています。
病院経営サポートでは、提携医療法人のニーズを踏まえ、事業計画の策定から病床機能の転換、臨床業務の効率化、資金調達、人事労務体制の最適化、医材・医薬品の調達および購買、医療施設等の建築・改修、事業承継まで幅広く支援しています。 コンサルティングでは、病院経営サポートを通じて蓄積してきた豊富な知見・経験に基づき、それぞれの病院が抱える多様な課題の解決に貢献します。
高齢者向け住宅では、アクティブな未来志向な方に先進的でホスピタリティ溢れるサービスを創造しています。入居される方の要望に単に応えるだけでなく、その先の感動とサプライズ、ワクワクする人生へとつなげることを目指しています。 介護施設紹介では、入居者およびご家族の希望に沿った施設を紹介するだけでなく、入居の手続きや引っ越し、在宅生活の見守りや家事代行など、サービスの拡充を進めています。
医療・介護 DX では、過重労働や人手不足、業務の属人化など、現場が抱える構造的な課題解決に向け、業務の可視化、プロセスの標準化を踏まえてDX推進を支援します。 医療データでは、医療機関の匿名加工された電子カルテデータを独自のアルゴリズムで解析し、活用しています。

about: Bienvenido a Capital Cell, la plataforma líder en inversión alternativa de Europa para el sector de la Biotecnología y las Ciencias de la Vida.

En Capital Cell creemos en el poder de las inversiones inteligentes para dar forma a un futuro mejor para todos. Seleccionadas por expertos y respaldadas por líderes de la innovación, te ofrecemos la oportunidad única de estar a la vanguardia de la revolución biotecnológica. Nuestra misión es democratizar el acceso a inversiones de alto impacto y rentabilidad en las ciencias de la vida, haciendo posible que cualquiera pueda contribuir al próximo gran avance en la salud humana.

Capital Cell nació en 2015 en el ecosistema científico de Barcelona, y desde entonces se ha convertido en uno de los mayores inversores en empresas emergentes biotecnológicas de Europa, siempre con la ambición de impulsar globalmente la innovación en salud y biotecnología.

Contamos con una red global de más de 3.500 científicos, médicos y expertos en inversión para examinar y seleccionar meticulosamente sólo las empresas más prometedoras. Sólo el 3% de las empresas que se ponen en contacto con nosotros llegan a nuestra plataforma, lo que garantiza que tus inversiones están en las mejores manos.

Nos entusiasma formar parte de un sector biotecnológico que evoluciona rápidamente. Las empresas en las que invertimos desarrollan diagnósticos, tratamientos y herramientas de vanguardia que tienen el potencial de transformar la atención sanitaria a escala mundial.

Invertir con Capital Cell es algo más que obtener beneficios económicos: es hacer una contribución significativa a la sociedad. Nuestra plataforma te permite apoyar investigaciones científicas pioneras que puedan mejorar vidas en todo el mundo, y generar valor para toda la sociedad.

Creemos que todo el mundo debería tener la oportunidad de invertir en biotecnología y ciencias de la vida. Nuestra plataforma minimiza las barreras de entrada, permitiendo a inversores privados individuales participar junto a fondos de inversión especializados e inversores especializados.
Biólogo reconvertido a emprendedor y financiero, Daniel Oliver es el fundador de Capital Cell.

home: Your climate partner in a changing world

We are global climate transition experts who deliver effective sector-wide and cross-sector solutions for our partners and the systems they operate in to accelerate the transition towards a prosperous, resilient, low carbon future.

Over the past two and a half decades, the Carbon Trust has partnered with businesses, governments, financial institutions and philanthropies to address some of the world's most complex climate and energy challenges across sectors and regions.

We are global climate transition experts who deliver effective sector-wide and cross-sector solutions for our partners and the systems they operate in to accelerate the transition towards a prosperous, resilient, low carbon future. For over 25 years, we have joined the dots across sectors around the world.
We look to bodies like the Carbon Trust that are rigorous and transparent. We’re thankful to have had their trusted expertise and are proud to have earned their verification.

Working with the Carbon Trust has enabled us to detangle the complexity of our supply chain. Thanks to their scalable model, we now have a much more detailed picture of where we are in meeting Kellogg’s ™ Better Days Promise environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy climate ambitions. The team's training sessions were especially helpful. We now have a better understanding on where to reduce our supply chain emissions and can factor our calculations into future procurement decisions.

We have worked closely with the Carbon Trust over a number of years and we are pleased to see our collective efforts come to fruition. Our broader sustainability agenda has developed from energy efficiency in our operations, to carbon, renewable energy, water and waste reduction, through to our supply chain goals.

We’re proud Virgin Media O2 is one of the first companies in the UK to be recognised by the Carbon Trust for our commitment to achieve Net Zero carbon emissions across our business, operations, and supply chain by the end of 2040.

Our experts provide trusted, hands-on support, combining strategic insight and technical expertise to deliver measurable climate impact. As an independent, purpose-driven organisation with over 25 years of experience, we reinvest our profits into accelerating the transition to a low carbon economy.

about: Invest for Circularity, Value, and Impact
Circulate Capital launched in 2018 to invest in solutions for the ocean plastic crisis in South and Southeast Asia.
Urgency and opportunity pushed us to broaden our investment focus to plastic circularity , including disruptive innovations across value chains, throughout the world’s high-growth markets .

We believe the circular economy is essential to tackling the world’s most urgent challenges – including protecting the environment, combating the climate crisis, improving health and livelihoods, and reducing inequality.

Circulate Capital was founded in 2018 to invest in high-potential companies that divert plastic waste from landfills and toward a circular future. Initially focused on ocean plastic pollution in South and Southeast Asia, the magnitude of the global waste crisis has pushed us to expand our focus. Our goal is to unlock capital to build circular supply chains for a sustainable future, while delivering competitive returns to investors.

Building the circular economy requires a systemic approach, supported by both upstream and downstream investment strategies. In addition to capital, we bring supply chain expertise and connections to help our investees scale their businesses and to catalyze further investments.

We are backed by the world’s leading corporations, including PepsiCo, Procter & Gamble, Dow, Danone, Chanel, Unilever, The Coca-Cola Company, Chevron Phillips Chemical Company LLC, and Mondelēz International. They offer invaluable insights, access to new markets, and commercial opportunities for our investees.

Circulate Capital also leverages blended finance vehicles to invest alongside development finance institutions and other private investors. This investment structure de-risks otherwise risky opportunities and places different types of investors shoulder-to-shoulder in the push towards circularity.

Most Companies Never Close a Round. Here’s Why.

Collectively, venture capital and private equity firms fund less than 0.05% of startups and less than 1.5% of early-stage companies seeking investment. For the small fraction that do receive Venture Capital (VC), the founders collectively receive less than 2% of all venture capital available, and more often than not, they lose voting control of their company.

The problem isn’t a lack of capital. It’s a lack of companies engineered to receive it.

Institutional investors are forcing VC firms to return capital because there aren’t enough quality companies to invest in. The gap is not supply, it is quality deal flow.
Most founders lack the securities law knowledge, capital structure expertise, and corporate engineering skills to create a Wall Street-worthy offering. That is what we fix.

home: Novella Center for Entrepreneurship Inc. (Novella Center) is a nonprofit 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to expanding access to the opportunity of entrepreneurship for all . Leveraging a decade of learning from our work at the Conscious Venture Lab, Novella Center creates partnerships and programming that help entrepreneurs rethink the relationship between business and society and build companies that matter.

Novella Center is named after our founder’s Mom, Joyce Novella Cherry. Joyce grew up in the 1940’s in segregated Baltimore, Maryland, and experienced firsthand the consequences of discrimination. She taught Jeff and his sisters about the importance of justice in all forms – legal, social, and particularly economic – and about how these were critical components for thriving communities. Particularly for those communities that have been historically neglected.

Today, Novella Center honors Joyce’s legacy through economic empowerment in those communities . We expose under-estimated entrepreneurs, early-stage founders, and CEOs to Stakeholder Theory and the Tenets of Conscious Capitalism™ and show them how managing a business for all stakeholders creates both societal and financial value, helps to create generational wealth, and ultimately leads to a more just, joyous, equitable, sustainable, and prosperous society for all.

about: Krishna Visvanathan and Scott Sage set out on a “there’s got to be a better way” adventure. Their vision was simple but bold: to build a venture firm that would stand shoulder to shoulder with early-stage founders—not just as investors, but as true partners through the hardest and most defining moments of company building.

This isn’t a tagline. It’s the way we work. We back founders from day one, working alongside them to unlock solutions, delivering unwavering hands-on support. When the path gets tough, we lean in harder. We stay in the trenches and see every project through, no matter the obstacles or complications.

“Good enough” just isn’t in our vocabulary. We believe in bold thinking and relentless persistence, and will dig deeper until the job is done. We use creativity to challenge convention and turn fresh ideas into game-changing solutions.

Breakthroughs come when we leave our comfort zones behind. We create space for both founders and our team to grow on a personal level, so we can all succeed on a collective one. We never stop asking “why?” or “what if?” to inspire innovation. And we aren’t afraid to reflect and adapt — because better awareness makes for better partners.

Technology may change the world, but people are the ones who shape it. That’s why we lead with empathy, honesty, and humility, creating a culture where everyone can be heard and feels confident enough to take risks. When we face difficult truths or choices, we make space for tough conversations and brave action. We put founders and teammates first, measuring our success by the growth and achievements of others.

While much of the venture industry is becoming smaller and more concentrated, we're expanding our reach. We believe outlier founders can emerge anywhere, so we're building one firm across Europe, North America, APAC, India, and beyond. Genius knows no borders. Neither should conviction.

We believe talent is evenly distributed. Opportunity is not. That's why we actively seek founders beyond the usual networks and geographies, backing exceptional people before consensus forms. We don't wait for founders to find us. We go to them.

We invest in the building blocks of the future: the foundational technologies that make everything else possible. From AI infrastructure and semiconductors to developer innovations, enterprise systems, and hard tech, we partner with founders solving difficult problems that require patience, technical depth, and long-term conviction.

home: Colin Walsh established Crescent Capital as a venture capital fund manager in 1995 in conjunction with Hambros plc, the Industrial Development Board for Northern Ireland (the predecessor to Invest NI) and a range of institutional and private investors from the UK, Europe and US, raising a £14m fund in 1996. This fund invested in 12 companies.

In 2004, Crescent raised its second fund, Crescent Capital II LP (‘Fund II’), at £22.5m in collaboration with Invest NI and the private sector including participation from Northern Ireland’s two universities (Queen’s University Belfast and Ulster University), the Northern Ireland Local Government Officers Superannuation Committee, Ulster Bank Limited, the European Investment Fund and the New York State Common Retirement Fund (‘NYSCRF’). This fund completed investments in 14 businesses, including one crossover investment from the first fund.

In 2013, Crescent raised its third fund, Crescent Capital III LP (‘Fund III’), at £30m in collaboration with Invest NI, NYSCRF (via 57 Stars), Queen’s University Belfast and several private investors. This fund completed investments in 15 companies, including two crossovers from the second fund.

Crescent completed investments in 38 companies across these funds. Crescent considers that some of Northern Ireland’s most exciting technology companies, which are at the forefront of the development of the local indigenous technology sector, have emerged from these portfolios. Returns have also been achieved from investments in industrial and manufacturing businesses.

Across these portfolios were several companies widely regarded as being among the most promising businesses with substantial international export potential. Several of these companies achieved significant progress in sales, profitability, employment, and shareholder value.
All the investments in the three funds are either exited and/or, in the case of Fund III, distributed to partners.

about: Drug discovery demands a model that delivers more often. Here’s our standard.
Investing at Inception to De-risk and Set Companies up for Success

Cure is focused on de novo company formation. We closely collaborate with visionary scientists to identify breakthrough ideas that have the potential to become exceptional companies. We know great ideas need funding to prove their feasibility and seeding allows us to work alongside entrepreneurs on key experiments that validate, explore, and de-risk the underlying science. Navigating the seed phase together increases value for entrepreneurs, illuminates the best path for clinical development, and sets the foundation for success.
Increasing the Probability of Success and Mitigating the Cost of Failure

Genetic validation provides a knowledge disparity that increases our probability of success. We understand this information must be embraced as an iterative process to guide drug candidates through development. Unbiased genetic validation can clarify a drug’s mechanisms of action, as well as its efficacy, toxicity, and patient population. The revolutionary ideas we invest in provide broad opportunities and may inspire innovations across multiple diseases and drug modalities when guided by continuous genetic validation.
Guiding Day-to-Day Decisions and Building Alongside Entrepreneurs

When we invest, we invest more than capital. Our people follow-through by getting our hands dirty in the company building trenches, collaborating with entrepreneurs, and operationalizing capital to become a true sweat equity partner. We embed world-class industry veterans to work alongside entrepreneurs and guide the company’s growth towards its next milestone and its own team of A-list talent. Out of the utmost respect for people and the science, we vote with our feet to bring patients suffering life-altering diseases closer to life-changing cures.
We Create With Entrepreneurs, For Patients

That’s why we work alongside entrepreneurs to impart lessons learned from a proud legacy of landmark labs, breakthrough discoveries, and historic companies. With a culture founded on respect and a level-headed devotion to scientific fact, we bring those suffering life-altering diseases closer to life-changing cures.

Debiopharm is an independent biopharmaceutical company based in Switzerland with an ongoing commitment to develop tomorrow’s standard of care to cure cancer & infectious diseases and improve patient quality of life. Our main activities include drug development, drug manufacturing and digital health investment.
For more than 45 years, we have been driven by the same commitment: bringing innovative solutions to patients

Our story began in 1979 when Dr. Rolland-Yves Mauvernay, convinced that many useful therapeutic products were abandoned before reaching their full potential, decided to establish Debiopharm, a company dedicated to in-licensing innovative compounds and developing them into medicines for out-licensing. Having launched this unique business model with a staff of only 2 people, today, Debiopharm’s 420 employees are now active in a variety of roles within drug development, drug manufacturing and investment in digital health and smart data start-ups.

Together with his son Thierry Mauvernay, they were able to build a team of dedicated professionals with a broad range of expertise. Debiopharm is now a group of three companies active in drug development (Debiopharm International), drug manufacturing (Debiopharm Research & Manufacturing) and digital health investment (Debiopharm Innovation Fund). Debiopharm is the Life Science division of our parent company Après-demain SA, active in asset diversification and philanthropy.

about: NEW ZEALAND’S LEADING PRIVATE COMPANY INVESTOR
Established in 1994, Direct Capital has been at the forefront of developing New Zealand’s private equity industry.

Direct Capital is itself a private company, owned by its executives. We understand the issues that business owners think about when considering how to grow their business or facilitate a change of ownership. Investing in private companies is all we do and it's all we've done for over 30 years.
The common perception of what’s become known collectively as private equity is that all investors have the same style and business model. But the reality is very different.

Some investors follow a “leverage model”, relying on debt to produce financial returns. This can be successful over short periods of the economic cycle but it doesn’t work forever. Some investors are “control” focussed but that only works if you’re also running the company.

Our returns come from investing in growth creating permanent value. We invest and become partners with owners and management running good companies and we act the same whether we are a 20% shareholder or an 80% shareholder.

Paddy joined Direct Capital in 2023, following two years at PwC working in Corporate Finance advisory. He has experience in M&A, valuation, financial modelling and due diligence. Paddy's role includes assisting with the evaluation of investment opportunities, transaction execution, research and investee company support.
Rosalie joined Direct Capital in January 2018 as Finance Manager. Rosalie is a Chartered Accountant with ten years experience in accounting roles.

home: WHY GROWTH CAPITAL CAN MAKE ALL THE DIFFERENCE

New Zealand has a wealth of successful, privately owned businesses. But many owners still get caught up in the day to day operations and forget about the bigger picture – such as enhancing growth options, acquiring a competitor, expanding to Australia, or thinking about their plans beyond business. This is where Direct Capital can help.

Direct Capital invests in the New Zealand and Australian mid-market private company sector in expansion, succession and pre-IPO situations. We typically invest between $30 - $100m of equity into companies and are comfortable with both minority and majority shareholdings.

בתחילת שנות ה-2000 התחילה לחלחל ההבנה ששינוי האקלים עומד לשנות את פני כדור הארץ ואת חיי בני האדם. בשנת 2007 הגענו למסקנה שאנחנו יכולים לעשות משהו אחר וטוב יותר, לכן הקמנו את חברת דוראל.

home: קבוצת דוראל היא חברה יזמית מובילה בתחום האנרגיה המתחדשת, הפועלת משנת 2007 בישראל ובעולם.

לחברה מאות מתקנים מניבים והיא ממשיכה להקים ולהוציא לפועל פרויקטים רבים וגדולים המשלבים אנרגיה סולארית ואגירת אנרגיה. לצד פרויקטים אלה, דוראל מקימה את המתקן הראשון בישראל לייצור מימן ירוק ומובילה את התחום עם השקעות והסכמים ארוכי טווח, במסגרת זרוע ההשקעות והחדשנות שלה.
דוראל מספקת חשמל ללקוחות עסקיים מובילים במסגרת הרפורמה במשק החשמל.
קבוצת דוראל היא החברה המובילה בישראל בייזום ובהקמת פרויקטים להפקת חשמל מאנרגיית שמש ולאגירת אנרגיה, ולה מאות מתקנים מניבים ברחבי המדינה.
דוראל מקדמת פרויקטים משמעותיים בדנמרק בשותפות עם שחקנים מקומיים מובילים בעלי ניסיון רב בשוק הסולארי המקומי והגלובלי. לאחרונה הפעילה את המתקן URUP בהספק 60 MWp.
תחום האנרגיה המתחדשת באיטליה מציע הזדמנויות רבות להשתלבות בשוק המקומי, ודוראל מקדמת פרויקטים סולאריים ואגרו-וולטאיים. הבחירה בכמה ערוצי פעילות מייצרת עבור החברה אופק לשגשוג בשוק המקומי.

פעילותה של דוראל בשוק האנרגיה האמריקאי נעשית באמצעות Doral Renewables LLC. החברה מפתחת עשרות פרויקטים ופעילה בלמעלה מ-20 מדינות בארה"ב. הפרויקט הגדול ביותר שדוראל מקימה נכון להיום הוא Mammoth Solar במדינת אינדיאנה המתפרש על פני שטח של כ-50 אלף דונם והספקו 1.6 גיגה-ואט.
