Intersouth Partners, the oldest venture capital firm in North Carolina's Research Triangle region, is also one of the oldest in the Southeast. Like other entrepreneurial endeavors, Intersouth had relatively humble beginnings. Dennis Dougherty and Roy Rodwell founded the first Intersouth fund in 1985 with just $6.4 million in committed capital. They believed that entrepreneurship would be an important part of the successful growth of the Research Triangle and North Carolina and that a venture fund located in and focused on the region would help catalyze that growth.

Dougherty was introduced to Eugene Kleiner, founder of the pioneer venture firm Kleiner, Perkins, Caulfield and Byers. Mr. Kleiner joined Intersouth as a Special Limited Partner and Chairman of the first Intersouth Advisory Board. He remained active with the firm until his retirement in 1998.
Intersouth Partners II was raised in 1989. Shortly thereafter, the firm added a third partner, Mitch Mumma, who had been involved in several of Intersouth's portfolio companies as a CFO.

Whether it’s the first million or hundreds of millions, Invoke is comfortable to back winners.
We provide unrivalled technological, operational and commercial expertise gained through decades of building world-leading British technology companies such as Autonomy, Blinkx and Darktrace.

about: Around 2018, Italy started to change. Not loudly, not all at once, but consistently. A new wave of companies emerged, some built in Italy, others built abroad by Italian founders who hadn't cut their ties. Capital started flowing again. International funds began showing up on cap tables. Still, the real shift wasn't visible in pitch decks or press releases. It was happening in WhatsApp groups, at late dinners, on weekend trips that somehow turned into informal board meetings. Founders started talking to each other. Really talking.

By 2022, it was no longer unusual to see seed rounds made up almost entirely of founders. No big institutions. No elaborate processes. Just experienced entrepreneurs backing other entrepreneurs early, often before anything looked "institutional-grade". Many of them were second-time founders. They had scars. They had pattern recognition. This didn't happen because someone designed it. It happened because the ecosystem was finally mature enough to support it.
IF THIS TRUST WAS REAL, IT DESERVED A VEHICLE

At a certain point, the need became obvious. If this energy was real, it deserved structure. Not to slow it down. Not to institutionalize it into irrelevance. But to amplify it. The idea was simple: create a vehicle that could channel this founder-to-founder momentum, while adding the discipline, governance and international standards of venture capital. A Founders Fund — built by founders, for founders.
KOINOS, LORENZO, AND THE MOMENT EVERYTHING ALIGNED

That's when Koinos Capital SGR entered the story. Some founders in the community had already backed Lorenzo Franzi in previous ventures. He had been an entrepreneur, an angel investor, and later an investor at Global Founders Capital. He was ready to return with a clear ambition: bring that mindset back home. Not as nostalgia. As strategy. A founder community that already trusted each other. An institutional platform built for the long term. An investment team grounded in global experience.

Italian Founders Fund did not start as a financial product. It started as an answer to a question founders were already asking: what would happen if we built the fund we always wished we had? We are committed to share that journey. The thinking behind the investments. The trade-offs that never appear in press releases. The reality of building venture capital in a country that is finally finding its rhythm. We are sharing this for the same reason we built it: ecosystems improve when people share what actually happens.
italianfoundersfund.com.desc: Italian Founders Fund backs entrepreneurs with Italian roots and global ambitions — a community-driven venture fund managed by Koinos Capital.
home: Do you want to share your business idea with us?

Jet HR is building a modern payroll and HR platform for Italian SMBs, an under-digitized market worth an estimated €2.8bn in Italy alone. The company was founded by Marco Ogliengo, second-time founder and former CEO of ProntoPro, scaled into a leading European marketplace before its acquisition by Immobiliare.it, and Francesco Scalambrino, former VP Product at ProntoPro and later Product Director at PayFit and Oyster, leading payroll products in regulated markets.

Sava is developing next-generation biosensing technology that enables continuous, painless and real-time access to biological signals, in the rapidly expanding wearable biosensor and continuous glucose monitoring market, projected to reach $20B by 2028. The company was founded by Renato Circi and Rafael Michali, bioengineering graduates from Imperial College London who previously built Caura together before launching Sava in 2019.

Mama Health is a patient intelligence platform that captures and structures longitudinal patient voice, converting fragmented qualitative data into structured, reusable datasets for pharma companies. The company was founded by Mattia Marco Caruson, who previously co-founded Teach&Touch, a rehabilitation app for children, and Dr. Jonas Witt, a medical doctor and former researcher at the Max Planck Institute.

When we look to the future, we envision abundance – an abundance of wellbeing and vitality shared by everyone on the planet. about: K9 Ventures is a technology-focused Pre-Seed fund in Palo Alto, California.

K9 Ventures is a technology focused Pre-Seed fund based in Palo Alto, California. We believe that extraordinary things are possible when great teams come together around technology. We primarily invest at the pre-seed stage, when the founding team is established and just starting to build the product, but we sometimes invest even earlier and have engaged with founders when they’re just thinking about the idea and haven’t yet incorporated their company.

K9 wants to be the first institutional / professional capital raised by the companies we invest in. This means we typically engage with companies either when they have raised no capital at all (preferred) or when they have raised only friends and family money. If a company is going through an incubator / accelerator, then that’s probably already too late for K9 to engage.

Our initial investment can range between $250K and $750K, with the sweet-spot being around $400K. We prefer to lead investment rounds, and when we do, K9 will take a board seat and actively work with the founder(s) to build the company. To provide sufficient attention to each portfolio company, K9 only invests in 4-6 companies per year. We structure all our investments as priced equity rounds based on the Series Seed documents (or the more recent fork at Cooley Go ) and do not do Convertible Notes /SAFEs. To learn more, please see our investment criteria .

VC firms love to talk about how important they are to their portfolio companies’ success. We don’t believe in singing our own praises. If you want to learn how we’ve helped entrepreneurs like you, we encourage you to talk to startup founders in the K9 portfolio .
Our view is that money is a commodity in the venture capital industry and the only two currencies that matter are reputation and time . With that in mind, our four guiding values are:
To get to know us better, please read our blog — we’re open with our opinions and and consistent in our views.

Dogs have many traits that can be useful at different times. They can be your best friend; they can be loyal and loving, aggressive and intelligent. Startups require different forms of support at different times. If dogs are “man’s best friend,” you can think of K9 Ventures as the “startup’s best friend.”

about: T ej Kohli is the Chairman of Kohli Ventures. He is the former founder of a series of companies clustered around the development of payment gateways and fraud protection services for high-risk online sectors during the dot com boom. In the early 2000’s his companies dominated the high-risk online payments sector and employed hundreds of software engineers in India and Costa Rica.

His first major liquidity event was in 2006. This happened when Tej Kohli sold one of the companies in the first of what later became a series of high-value trade sales. Tej Kohli used the proceeds from the sales and their multiple years of earn-out liquidity to formally establish three organisations: The Tej Kohli Foundation , Zibel Real Estate and Kohli Ventures.

Born in Delhi, India, Tej Kohli’s lifelong interest in technology started when he graduated in Electrical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur in 1980. In 1981 he moved to California when his mother, who was one of the first female Diplomats in the Indian Government, was posted to the USA.

Tej Kohli enjoyed prodigious early success in California as a real estate investor, acquiring multi-unit residential buildings from failed Savings & Loan institutions at cents on the dollar and re-selling the units individually to the sitting tenants. Later the company would collapse amid an investigation into one of its projects, which led to a fall from grace for Tej.

​It was 1999 when Tej Kohli found himself in Costa Rica amidst the excitement of the dot com boom. He founded a company specialising in building payment gateways with teams of developers in Costa Rica and India, which quickly grew into a conglomerate of companies that he sold from 2006 onwards. This major liquidity event was an important milestone which facilitated a life transition from entrepreneur to investor and philanthropist.

As a philanthropist, Tej Kohli has instigated and funded grassroots projects targeting a range of global health issues, most notably by funding treatment interventions that have cured tens of thousands of people of corneal and cataract blindness in some of the world’s most deprived communities. Tej Kohli has also funded innovative research for the prevention and cure of blindness.

​As an investor, Tej Kohli has invested across a variety of verticals, most notably in artificial intelligence, robotics and eSports. Today Tej Kohli is Europe’s biggest individual eSports investor and he continues to back ventures through Kohli Ventures.

Tej Kohli formed Kohli Ventures to provide an efficient vehicle for the investment of the incoming liquidity arising from earn-out provisions attached to the sale of companies such as Estacion Tramar. Kohli Ventures’ investment criteria are unique because Tej Kohli prefers to be the sole investor in a venture, working directly alongside founders and continuing to fund all future funding requirements as well as providing substantial intellectual capital support until an exit is achieved.

For the past decade, the most valuable technology companies were built in bits. As the barriers around general software fall, the next durable advantages are moving into the physical world, with systems that cannot be copied at near-zero cost.

Manufacturing, energy, logistics, and infrastructure form the backbone of the global economy. Recent technological advances in AI, robotics, sensing, and advanced compute make it possible to bring intelligence into traditional industries. For the first time, the world of atoms can be engineered with the speed once reserved for bits.
Design cycles are compressing, but bringing systems into production remains complex, calling for investors with a deep understanding of industrial value chains and operations.

The pressure to rebuild is rising. Europe combines world-leading research with global industrial leadership. Institutions like ETH Zurich and VTT push the frontier in robotics, quantum systems, and advanced materials, while proximity to deep industrial heritage allows technologies to be tested, iterated, and validated in real operating environments.
These forces of technological advancement, urgency, and the sheer magnitude of the opportunity rarely align.
Welcome to the early stage of a new industrial era.
Europe, anchored in the Nordics and DACH

home: MDR Lab is Mishcon de Reya's home for legal innovation – the place where lawyers, clients and the technology industry come together to work out what's next in law and start building it. For over a decade we've sat at that intersection, turning early experiments and R&D into the tools, relationships and ways of working that shape how legal services are delivered today.
We started as one of the UK’s first LegalTech incubators. Today, we train General Counsel, advise clients on AI, build our own AI solutions, and back the founders reshaping the legal industry.
Launched the UK’s first incubator and investment programme in 2016, bringing early stage legaltech companies into the firm to build alongside practicing lawyers.

Supported dozens of companies over multiple cohorts to launch and scale as their partner, customer, and sometimes, investor. Notable alumni include Laurel, ThirdFort, Orbital Witness, DraftWise and Ayora.
We built a machine learning and data science function in 2017 allowing us in 2023, as the Legal Sector embraced AI, to make a fast start in building in-house AI tools, including deReyAI.
We were one of the first UK firms to deploy Legora and remain a key design partner of theirs, including on their Portals which enabled AI-collaboration with clients.

Together with Flex and Mishcon Academy, we launched the GC Academy to provide GCs and senior in-house with the skills and networks to run a legal function and continue to advise our clients on how to use technology for strategic impact.

Each step laid the foundation for the next. The incubator gave us the relationships and the product insight; the investments sharpened our judgment; and a decade experimenting with emerging technology at the frontier of law and technology gives us our competitive edge.
We build and experiment with AI and technology. We stay wired into the legaltech market, then bring that insight to our lawyers and clients to drive better outcomes.

A hands-on development programme for General Counsel and senior in-house lawyers, built with Flex Legal. Four modules, one goal: to give our alumni the skills and network to run a modern legal function. Over 100 in-house lawyers have so far been through the programme.

about: Our Mission Robin Hood elevates New Yorkers out of poverty by funding, supporting, and connecting high-impact community organizations, partnering with government, and advocating for what works so that New York City can be an engine of upward mobility for all.

It takes an army to fight poverty, and we are uniquely positioned to build one. We have a deep-seated reputation for partnering across sectors and convening a wide array of influencers – celebrities, elected officials, financial and industry leaders, and more – to create an unmatched coalition for change so that New York City can be an engine of upward mobility for all.

Inspired by a shared love for NYC, Robin Hood was created over a dinner of Chinese takeout by board members Paul Tudor Jones, Peter Borish, David Saltzman, and Glenn Dubin, along with Maurice Chessa. Their mission? Fighting poverty by adapting investment principles to charitable giving. Our first grants were made to the Association to Benefit Children and the Children’s Health Fund, totaling $52,000.
1991-1993 Pioneers in the fight against AIDS
Robin Hood established a life-saving needle-exchange program and awarded our first housing grant to Housing Works and Harlem United to support New Yorkers living with HIV.

The Robin Hood Relief Fund was created to help those devastated by the 9/11 terrorist attacks, and distributed more than $65M to organizations supporting families, survivors, and New York’s recovery. The Fund was reactivated during Superstorm Sandy in 2012, and again in 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic. To date, the Fund has distributed over $230 million in aid to frontline organizations across the city.

about: First Private Equity Firm Singularly Focused on Investments in Middle Market Aerospace and Defense Businesses

Liberty Hall Capital Partners was founded in 2011 as the first private equity firm singularly focused on investments in middle market businesses serving the global aerospace and defense industry. Utilizing our “hands-on”, demonstrated and repeatable investment strategy, we seek to transform middle market aerospace and defense companies into larger, more capable and diverse strategic assets.

Through implementation of our research-driven investment strategy, we seek to identify segments within the global aerospace and defense industry with above market growth and differentiated risk-return characteristics. While we are aerospace and defense sector specialists, we are business model agnostic; we target suppliers and manufacturers, aircraft financiers, distributors and MRO service providers and software and technology companies serving the aerospace, defense and space end markets.

Based in Charleston, South Carolina, Liberty Hall has a demonstrated track record of acquiring, integrating and building global businesses. Our 24 acquisitions include businesses located in the United States (14 acquisitions), United Kingdom (4), Germany (2), Australia, Austria, Israel and New Zealand. Our current and former portfolio companies support every significant commercial aerospace, defense and space platform and serve global OEMs and defense primes across over 300 airlines, 1,000 helicopter operators and 11,500 business jet owners.

Since November 2013, Liberty Hall has invested over $1.2 billion in equity capital in 24 acquisitions of businesses serving the global aerospace and defense industry, including 8 platform and 16 add-on acquisitions.

Liberty Hall seeks to transform middle market aerospace and defense businesses into larger, more capable and diverse strategic assets using a hands-on, research-driven and repeatable investment strategy.

home: Lightsmith is the world’s first growth equity investor in adaptation and resilience, founded in 2017.

Yet adaptation and resilience (A&R) remains significantly under-invested, making up just 5% of tracked global climate finance. Leading institutions including BCG/Temasek, GIC/Bain, and McKinsey now project the A&R investment opportunity will exceed $1 trillion by 2030.

Lightsmith was one of the first investors to identify the adaptation and resilience investment opportunity, completing an initial mapping of A&R market segments in 2017 that totaled $170 billion in annual spending. Lightsmith launched what experts consider the first private equity fund for adaptation and resilience in 2019 ( Climate Policy Initiative, 2022 ). By 2024, Lightsmith’s same A&R market segments had grown to $480 billion, a ~20% compound annual growth rate that doubled initial projected growth rates.

After nearly a decade of market analysis and eight investments in Fund I [Learn About Our Portfolio] , Lightsmith has refined its investment focus to two priority focus areas: Infrastructure & Energy Resilience and Supply Chain Resilience.

Infrastructure & Energy Resilience and Supply Chain Resilience are market segments where spending has shifted from reactive disaster-recovery to proactive risk mitigation, resilience, and efficiency. Lightsmith conducts continuous research to identify what focus areas are in the “Near Horizon”, where companies and communities have moved to proactive spending on technologies and solutions that support resilience and adaptation to the increasing risk, impact, and complexity of climate change.
Lightsmith partners with A&R companies that demonstrate:
with significant revenues and customer validation
delivering attractive economics and clear paths to profitability
with durable competitive advantages in high growth markets
Lightsmith’s investment strategy combines deep-sector expertise, active partnership, and a proprietary framework for identifying companies positioned to lead the A&R economy.

home: Started as a small preseed fund in Poland in 2019, we quickly became one of the most active preseed/seed funds in all of Central Eastern Europe - with almost 40 companies in our portfolio.

We invest in great teams. You might not know everything, you might still be looking for your product market fit, you might be at the MVP stage. But you must be a team willing to spend the next few years transforming your vision into reality through blood, sweat and tears.

Socrates said "I know that I know nothing" - we value open-minded founders who listen to different arguments and are able to validate them fast as hypotheses. After all, it doesn't matter whose argument or idea it was. What should matter is if it works or not.

In general we don't invest in teams that are running multiple ventures. Of course there are individuals able to run a few companies at the same time, but you can't build Google, Apple and Facebook simultaneously. We need you to commit your time and mind.

It's almost certain that right now there are a few teams across the world which are building something very similar to what you are doing. You need to be able to put aside the backlog of 20 functionalities that you wanted to implement before going live and instead be able to check your assumptions as soon as possible. We love the pareto rule and lean approach. Great Example from buffer.com
The world is full of people who talk a lot about what they are going to do. We like them, but we invest in people who, instead of talking, roll up their sleeves and get down to work.
We add value through long-term commitment
Building great companies requires time - and we understand that. Although we invest at the pre-seed/seed stages we want to support you in the long term.

home: Tomorrow’s category leaders won’t just live behind screens. They’ll fundamentally rearrange the four building blocks of physical industry. Maniv backs the founders doing the work.

Manufacturing, reinvented The vehicles, materials, and hardware of tomorrow can no longer be built the way industrial-era factories built yesterday's. New manufacturing platforms, materials science, and production models are collapsing the cost and time it takes to bring physical products to market at scale.

The new physical network Getting people and goods from A to B is being rebuilt outside the constraints of legacy fleets, ownership models, and infrastructure. Autonomy, new vehicle formats, and smarter logistics networks are redrawing how movement happens on the ground, in the air, at sea, and in space.

Rewiring the grid For decades, energy meant flat demand, regulated returns, and slow-moving innovation. Now AI compute demands, EVs, and reindustrialization are straining the grid from every direction, and a once-conservative industry is investing at historic scale to keep pace.

Rethinking silicon Every smart factory, vehicle, and grid hides a tangle of silicon, circuits, and compute straining data centers and grids alike. Moore's Law, once declared dead, is being revived through new architectures, new memory, and processors built for ever-increasing computing demand.

about: I believe we can improve the planet and people’s lives without sacrificing our economic wellbeing. In my corporate career, I experienced first-hand how sensible clean air policies can significantly reduce pollution at a fraction of the projected cost to industry. And today, the renewable energy industry is one of the largest job creators in our modern economy. I’m confident we can overcome our greatest challenges — such as climate change and adaptation — cost-effectively by investing in people, fostering innovation, and increasing access to capital for early-stage companies.

In my 1.0 career, I held a number of executive positions at a Fortune 500 energy company, helping the organization grow its deregulated business from a start-up into an industry leader with a global footprint. I look back at the most challenging episodes of my career as the most rewarding. I apply my corporate experience and lessons learned to advise early-stage companies in many areas — including governance, organizational structure, strategy, fundraising, financial reporting, risk management, deal structuring and M&A.

I grew up all over the world, living in half a dozen countries before I turned ten. The diversity and cultural richness I experienced at an early age instilled in me the belief that we are all connected and part of one global community. I have served as Chair of UNICEF USA’s Mid-Atlantic regional board and member of its National Development Committee. I have also served on the honorary board of Halcyon, an incubator for social entrepreneurs and artists, and am currently an advisor to the Energy Analysis & Policy program at UW-Madison as well as a MERLIN mentor.

My academic background was in particle physics but when my doctoral project was canceled, I turned my attention to environmental issues. I've published several papers on climate change, clean air and renewable energy policy, which have been widely cited. I was born in London though I've always supported Liverpool FC, I speak three languages, and I’m a part-owner of a biodynamic farm in the UK. I've traveled all over the world and do not believe in coincidences.

about: MD Start is different from most incubators

Our mission is to incubate medical device innovation to the stage where it will be of interest to later stage investors (corporates and venture capital firms). Since MD Start was created in 2010, we have evaluated over 2000 inventions, worked on +50 projects and created 13 new companies.

MD Start is looking for ideas that are too early for large corporate or venture investors. Based in Paris, France, MD Start evaluates ideas from all over Europe and beyond, benefiting from a unique environment, where the vast majority of medtech inventions originate from, while very few entrepreneurs turn these medical device innovations into companies. We look for ideas that others miss and truly add value. We prove the technology by demonstrating the validity of the concept in a fast and capital efficient manner.

home: 医療機器開発は 医工連携だけでは成功が難しく、 ビジネス（商）の観点が不可欠です。
MedVenture Partners株式会社は 医療機器専門のベンチャーキャピタルです。 代表の大下 創、医師の池野 文昭を中心に 投資先医療機器ベンチャーの 成功を目指し、 豊富な経験とネットワークを活用した 支援を行っています。
臨床ニーズに基づくアイデアの 事業化を後押しし、 医療機器ベンチャーの エコシステムを活性化
現在の日本では臨床ニーズを解決する有望なアイデアが存在しながら、事業化や医療機器産業の発展につながらないという課題を抱えています。医療機器ベンチャーが取り組む製品開発、臨床試験、上市、そしてEXIT（医療機器メーカーによる買収／IPO）を経て、成功経験のある人材がまた起業していく。そんな医療機器ベンチャーのエコシステム活性化を目的としてMedVenture Partnersは設立されました。
経営を担う大下創、池野文昭の両名は日本の医療業界および、アメリカの医療機器ベンチャーのエコシステムにおいて長年の経験を有しています。現在も海外医療機器ベンチャーへの投資を積極的に実施しており、世界の医療機器の最新動向を把握しています。また、投資担当メンバーの多くは医療機器ビジネスの実務経験があります。
大下は、シリコンバレーにおいてFoxHollow Technologies、Chestnut Medical等に対しリードインベスターとして投資を行い、EXITに貢献しました。池野は、2001年以降200社を超える米国医療機器ベンチャーの研究開発、動物実験、臨床試験等に関与してきました。
医療機器を主としたライフサイエンス分野におけるベンチャー企業を投資対象としています。シード・アーリーからレイトステージまでの全ステージが投資対象です。
私たちは、「開発リスクは高く、販売リスクが低い医療機器開発を目指すベンチャー企業」への投資を重視しています。当社が投資判断を行う際の重要なポイントは、以下の6つです。
慢性鼻炎を治療するcryoablationデバイスの開発 （acquired by Stryker / FEB 2019）
血管内治療用医療機器(ステント、カテーテル等)の開発 （大塚ホールディングス傘下 株式会社JIMRO に買収されました）

about: Trust is built on evidence, not assertion. We form our own view of a team long before a round exists — and we don’t wait for the market to agree before we act on it.

Our work starts before the investment and continues through the decisions that shape what comes next. Two systems make that possible. Metis X is the platform we built in-house to find and evaluate teams early. Surge is our portfolio team and Venture Partners, who work alongside founders after we invest.
At pre-Series A there is rarely enough evidence in the business to justify a decision. There is almost always enough in the people.
An insight earned over years. Technical depth that’s hard to replicate. A team that knows how to build together.
We look for founders with an advantage they’ve earned—and the ambition to take it further. What have they built? What do they understand that others miss? How do they respond when the plan breaks?
Metis X connects the signals behind a team: what they’ve built, where their expertise comes from, and how the business is developing.

We built it in-house to develop our own coverage of the markets we invest in—helping us meet teams early, ask better questions and form an independent view . That work continues from first contact through exit.
Deep market knowledge. Room to lead across a region.

about: Not just a lab. Not just a network. A launchpad for the physical future.
Connecting entrepreneurs, manufacturers, and capital in one purpose-built space.
Powering the next generation of innovation

The next chapter of American innovation is being built in the physical world. As the U.S. reindustrializes and competes to lead in AI, advanced manufacturing, energy, and other emerging technologies, success will depend on the hardware, manufacturing systems, and critical infrastructure that underpin technologies. The mHUB platform combines facilities, networks, and capital so startups building for the physical world don't just survive, they scale.
mHUB removes barriers for hard tech founders and manufacturers

Every year, over 300 startups call mHUB home as they work to commercialize new physical products in energy, advanced manufacturing, quantum, healthcare, sustainability, and more. Innovators have access to state-of-the-art prototyping labs and a micro-factory. mHUB connects entrepreneurs with mentors, suppliers, and investors as well as opportunities to co-develop and pilot alongside industry. Further, mHUB Ventures makes direct investments in 20 - 30 startups every year.

Giving hardware and manufacturing due recognition as major drivers for prosperity and transformation, mHUB has built a community over 60,000 strong. From contractors and startups to corporates and philanthropists, mHUB has become a major force in consulting not just startups but also industry and investors on their own hard tech and manufacturing initiatives.
See how it all works in the most recent mHUB Annual Report.

Eight research-intensive university partners
Co-founded by eight research-intensive universities, collectively ranking number one for world-leading research power.
Investing in world-class research that become world-changing businesses

Midlands Mindforge is an ambitious, patient capital investment company co-founded by eight research-intensive universities in the Midlands. We invest in ground-breaking science and technology to build the businesses that bring it to market.

Through equity investment combined with hands-on company-building support, we create the conditions for spinouts and early-stage science and technology businesses to scale and thrive, right here in the Midlands.
The Midlands is home to clusters of outstanding research excellence

The Midlands was the birthplace of the first industrial revolution and is set to play a central role in turning the ambitions of the Modern Industrial Strategy into reality. Across its 20 universities, the region commands nationally significant strengths in engineering and manufacturing, life sciences and health technologies, AI, quantum, and clean energy. Together, these capabilities form a comprehensive commercialisation ecosystem, attracting £6bn in research funding between 2019 and 2024, and that has produced 352 IP-rich spinout businesses.

Equity investment into UK spinouts has grown at a 17.5% CAGR (2014–2024), and in 2024 UK spinout growth at seed stage was 2.1× that of other seed companies. Our goal is to build a highly collaborative spinout ecosystem throughout the region, creating a virtuous cycle of more spinouts attracting more talent, more growth, and more opportunities.
Mindforge targets early-stage science and technology businesses in three focus areas.

about: Learn more about Future Planet Capital Regional

For over 30 years, we have invested more than £100m into early-stage businesses and startups to help grow some of the West Midlands most exciting businesses. When partnering with us, you get more than money. We work with you to drive a growth strategy that will create value throughout your business and focus on the things that really matter.

We’re entrepreneurs ourselves and have a broad range of operational and strategic skills and expertise to help you see your business take off. With a hands-on approach, we can also help you find the right people to strengthen your team and support your business development activities to create a thriving business.
The Future Planet Capital Regional Journey

Future Planet Capital Regional (formerly known as Midven) was originally established as a venture capitalist firm by six Midlands-based entrepreneurs in 1990. The company went through a management buy-out in 2007, when the investment team acquired the business from the original founders.

Since then Future Planet Capital Regional became wholly owned by its management team, its grown quickly and solidly, more than doubling the team size and funds managed. To date, every fund that has been under Future Planet Capital Regional’s management has been regionally-focused.

In April 2021, Midven was acquired by Future Planet Capital. Future Planet Capital is a global venture capital and impact investor, connecting the world’s largest investors to the best minds in order to address global challenges. Future Planet Capital’s goal is to profitably solve the world’s greatest challenges in climate change, education, health, sustainable growth and security.
Andy joined Midven in 2018 taking on a role as portfolio manager.

経済産業省にて投資事業有限責任組合法、関連金融法制・税制・会社法制の改定を企画するなどベンチャー企業振興、産学連携施策等に従事。複数のベンチャー企業経営を経て、大手金融機関系VCにおいて国内外のベンチャー企業の投資開発及び経営支援に従事。 東京大学経済学部 卒業 コロンビア大学経営学修士（MBA） 京都大学 経営管理大学院 研究員 経済産業省「大学発ベンチャーのあり方研究会」 メンバー 国土交通省 i-Construction推進コンソーシアム企画委員会 委員 日本ベンチャーキャピタル協会（JVCA）理事・政策部会長

みやこキャピタル創業初期より参画し、ライフサイエンス・バイオ領域への投資を主導。創薬・医療機器分野において豊富な投資実績を持ち、アカデミア発スタートアップの事業化支援からEXITまでを一貫して担う。 7年間アカデミアで教員としてライフサイエンス分野の研究・指導に従事。 2002年日本アジア投資（JAIC）の子会社において再生医療・医療機器に特化したインキュベーション型ファンド創業期に参加、ファンドの設立から案件発掘、投資業務全般を担当。 2007年JAIC転籍後QOL関連分野の投資責任者・ファンドマネージャーを歴任。 再生医療、創薬から医療機器、健康関連サービスまで多くの投資を重ね、日本有数の成功実績を誇る。 Japan Venture Awards（JVA）2020 ベンチャーキャピタリスト奨励賞受賞。 埼玉大学大学院 修了、博士（理学）

みやこキャピタルのファウンダーとして創業を主導し、投資戦略の立案から案件発掘、ポートフォリオ企業の経営支援まで幅広く担う。大学・行政機関との強固な連携を基盤に、アカデミア発スタートアップの事業化を推進している。 30年以上一貫してベンチャー・中小企業の経営・投資事業に携わる。 1988年以来VC大手のジャフコにおいて投資部長、投資本部長等を歴任し、総額1,000億円以上のファンド組成・運営、100社を超える日本・米国・中国のベンチャー企業への投資・育成、上場・資本提携等に大きな成果をもたらした。 ジャフコ退職後、日本・中国関連のメディア・流通複合企業の経営陣としてグループ企業の設立・運営を行う傍ら、多くのベンチャー・中小企業の取締役等として事業構築・成長支援を実施。また複数の上場会社M&Aやセカンダリーファイナンスも手がけた。 横浜国立大学経済学部 卒業

みやこキャピタル創業初期からパートナーとして参画し、シリコンバレー拠点を軸に米国・グローバル市場へのアクセスを担う。長年の米国VC経験と幅広い国際ネットワークを活かし、投資先企業のグローバル展開を支援している。 1999年ジャフコ入社以降、ジェネラル・パートナーとして米国ファンド6本（総額約1,400億円）の設立・運営に携わり高いパフォーマンスを挙げた。 2003年からはJAFCO USA（現Icon Ventures）のCEOとしてジャフコ米国法人を再構築し、その後JAFCO USAは全米トップ25VCにランクイン（The Top 25 VC Firms 2013, AlwaysOn）、個人としても日本人初のトップ100キャピタリストに選ばれ（The Top 100 Venture Partners on the planet 2013, AlwaysOn)高い評価を受けた。 防衛大学校理工学部 卒業 山形大学 客員教授 九州大学 California Fellow

みやこ京大イノベーション2号ファンドの設立より、ディールソーシングからEXITまで投資業務全般を担当。主担当案件のIPO及びトレードセール実績を持つ。 当社入社以前は、外資系メーカーの技術職、環境・エネルギー専門コンサル会社の事業開発職を歴任後、ジャフコ入社。米中有力ベンチャーの日本進出を主導するとともに日本国内の有力ベンチャーの海外進出を数多く支援。中国ユニコーンベンチャー（その後上場）と日本上場企業の資本業務提携案件、日本企業の海外売却案件等実績を挙げ、ディールソーシング、事業性評価、投資・支援活動にも従事。 中国清華大学物理工学専攻 卒業 東京工業大学大学院修士課程（理工学） 修了 京都大学大学院博士課程（エネルギー経済分野） 指導認定退学

about: We are entrepreneurs and operators and have been working together for over 25 years.

We invest in enterprise software companies building mission-critical solutions for their customers that also have two additional characteristics (or plusses, as we call them) that are truly differentiating:

The first plus is technology that enables transformational, rather than incremental, change. The kind of technology that has the potential to materially impact the underlying value proposition within a specific domain. Technology that is so valuable in its own right that it is both a hedge against the company’s business model and a significant valuation multiplier.

The second plus refers to monetization strategies that go beyond typical SaaS licensing fees. Typically a byproduct of their business model, such companies have other inherent value that goes beyond traditional revenue. That value comes in the form of the unique and proprietary datasets they have created, the technical artifacts they have developed, or the network effect of an ecosystem.
We refer to the conversion of these two features as Software++, a combination that consistently gives companies a major competitive advantage while dramatically increasing their upside potential.
We are sector and vertical agnostic, and seek out high-performance companies
$1 million to $5 million (often the first institutional investor)

Wallenberg Investments administrerar Wallenbergstiftelserna samt förvaltar och utvecklar deras tillgångar. Stiftelsernas största tillgångar är det publika investmentbolaget Investor samt det privata ägarbolaget Wallenberg Investments. Förvaltningen bygger på aktivt ägande, en tradition som präglat familjen Wallenberg sedan 1856.

Genom långsiktigt direkt och indirekt ägande i företag med världsledande marknadspositioner, tillsammans med strategiska investeringar och aktiv portföljutveckling, skapar Wallenberg Investments hållbart värde och långsiktig avkastning. Wallenberg Investments samlar Stiftelsernas anslagsverksamhet, kapitalförvaltning och ägarstyrning i en gemensam organisation med fem investeringsenheter: Industrials, Real Assets, Alternative Funds, Special Investments och Ventures.

Wallenbergs kretslopp omfattar 16 allmännyttiga stiftelser – Wallenbergstiftelserna, investmentbolaget Investor samt ägarbolaget Wallenberg Investments. Genom långsiktig och engagerat ägande skapas avkastning som gör det möjligt för Stiftelserna att stödja grundforskning och utbildning som stärker Sverige över tid. Familjen Wallenberg är en aktiv del av kretsloppet genom sitt engagemang i styrelser, ägarfrågor och nätverk. I dag leds detta engagemang av familjemedlemmar ur femte generationen, med ett växande deltagande från den sjätte generationen.
Tillgångarna är uppdelade i fem investeringsenheter, från noterade industrier till tidiga ventures. Tillsammans spänner de över hela bolagets livscykel, med samma långsiktiga ägande som grund.
Långsiktigt ägande. Industriell excellens. Industrials utvecklar bolag som verkar inom industriell teknologi, avancerade system, tillverkning, material och digitala lösningar.

Reala tillgångar, för kommande generationer. Real Assets investerar i fysiska tillgångar med industriell koppling, såsom skog, mark och hållbar infrastruktur, där fokus ligger på förvaltning och utveckling av existerande innehav.
Strategiskt kapital utanför den publika marknaden. Alternative Funds investerar i onoterade fonder och, tillsammans med fondförvaltare eller andra betrodda partners, direkt i bolag som co-investors.

För morgondagens strategiska teknologier. Special Investments investerar i och utvecklar innovativa bolag i tidig tillväxtfas med bevisad marknadsrelevans, och bolag som bidrar med ett unikt värde till vårt kretslopp eller till det svenska samhällets strategiska förmågor.

about: Our conviction comes from experience applied with care. Case by case.
Newion is a venture firm from Amsterdam that has invested for over 25 years. That’s long enough to see how quickly markets change, and how good companies are built.

Those two speeds, how markets move, and how companies mature, create a familiar dynamic: growth can hide weak foundations, and tough markets surface them. Over time, the job becomes less about reacting to movement and more about understanding what will still work when conditions stop cooperating.

That’s the lens we bring to every conversation. We start with curiosity, then pressure-test coherence between the problem, the product, and a credible path to selling it. We look for compelling logic at the base of every company story: an underlying market shift, and people who can lead the journey.

And we stay close after the investment, too: not to run companies, but to help founders make the early calls that shape the next year: sequencing, trade-offs, perspectives. In the first 12–18 months, those decisions compound fast.

We invest at Seed and Series A , typically €1–10M , in rounds up to €20M, across European digital tech. Our team is compact and dedicated, so responsibility stays close to the work: we debate until the reasoning is clear, align, and move.
We use experience as leverage, not legacy.
We invest with the long term in mind. That means putting in the effort early, not after the round.

home: Leading the industry's response to climate change
OGCI is a CEO-led initiative focused on accelerating action to a net zero future consistent with the Paris Agreement.
At OGCI, we are proud of what we’ve done over the past decade to lead the industry’s ambition to reduce emissions in the timeframe of the Paris Agreement.

Since 2017, OGCI members have collectively reduced upstream operated methane emissions by 63%, cut routine flaring by 72% and invested $125 billion in low-carbon technologies and solutions, including renewables, biofuels and CCUS. We’ve shown what’s possible and we’re sharing what we’ve learned with companies outside our group to accelerate the global effort to achieve net zero.
OGCI’s 2026 Progress Report shows member companies met their collective 2025 upstream carbon intensity ambition and maintained methane intensity well below 0.20% for a fifth consecutive year.
Explore the latest performance data, the practical action behind the progress and the focus through 2030.

Hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide need to be captured and stored each year to achieve net zero. OGCI is working with industry, governments and other investors to scale up carbon capture, utilization and storage.

Eliminating methane emissions from oil and gas is a top priority for OGCI. That’s why we’re working to achieve near-zero methane emissions across the oil and gas industry and along the full gas value chain by 2030.

Decarbonizing hard-to-abate transport sectors such as shipping, aviation and trucking is crucial to achieve net zero. OGCI is working to develop low-carbon fuels such as biofuels, hydrogen and ammonia.

home: We are interested in technology companies in the fields of ICT, robotics and high-tech. We favor teams of professionals comprised or led by serial entrepreneurs with past growth, fundraising and/or exiting experience. We are looking for product building companies that would be high-potential, fast-growth, and ready to conquer foreign markets. Best time to talk us is just after first revenues in the company.

It all starts with a conversation where we learn about you and your ambition. In the space of few meetings we are targeting to decide whether to look further. We'll discuss particular terms, ask for more information, and analyse further. The legal part - we know everyone loves it, and, finally, we join your venture.

It is always best to reach to individual partners whom you feel will have the most relevant conversation with your team. It's advised for you to prepare to present your case in a convincing fashion - over presentation, executive summary, spreadsheet - or any other format that you feel does the job. Simplest way to start the process is by dropping us a line at hello@opencirclecapital.lt .

We are looking for ICT, Robotics and High-tech companies. We see ICT as broad field encompassing SaaS, marketplaces, apps, as well as infrastructure solutions. In Robotics we are looking at gadgets, logistics and warehousing, consumer electronics, industry 4.0 components, actuators, drone components. In High-tech, we are open to med-tech, optics, life-sciences, chemical innovations, and broader innovations.

We are looking to follow a successful company over several years with 4-5 investments totalling 3 million euros, however we prefer our initial investment to be much smaller in the space of 100-500 thousand euros. We are actively helping companies to raise money from co-investors at every round.
How much of shares are you looking to control?

We don't emphasize any particular shares target. As long as we can agree on a fair valuation, we take what the proportion is relative to the investment. We believe that throughout initial rounds the team should always maintain majority control of their company.

Beyond the capital provided we provide support to our companies with team building, business decisions, growth, technology transfer, and fundraising. We recognize that there is a degree of control that comes with our investment and we try to to balance it out so we are constructive and positive contribution to the companies.

We are happy with both. We prefer syndicated rounds and actively help our companies involve further investors. We can take the lead role, when it's needed, but also happy to follow if other investors are more active.
Is your investment limited by state support?

about: OrbiMed is a global investment firm that invests in companies engaged in the discovery and development of biopharmaceutical products, medical technologies, medical devices, diagnostics, drug discovery tools, and healthcare information technology and services companies.

The global healthcare industry sits at the intersection of several powerful long-term growth trends led by global demographics and the ineluctable advance of scientific innovation in treating disease.

These trends have caused a steady increase in the level of healthcare spending in the industrialized world, led by the U.S. which now spends over 17% of its GDP on healthcare. We believe the healthcare industry’s powerful growth profile coupled with its magnitude and complexity create myriad investment opportunities.

OrbiMed invests across the global healthcare industry, from seed-stage venture capital to large publicly-traded companies. Investments are made in one of three strategies: public equity, private equity, and private credit/royalty.

OrbiMed's private equity strategy is broad and flexible, investing from start-ups through growth equity. OrbiMed is typically a lead investor, helping to build our portfolio companies into market leaders. We invest globally, including across North America, Asia, and Europe.

OrbiMed provides commercial-stage healthcare companies with non-dilutive structured debt capital. Additionally, OrbiMed can monetize royalty streams, providing valuable financing solutions to owners of intellectual property.

OrbiMed manages a series of public equity funds, including long/short event-driven funds and closed-end investment trusts. We invest across all types of publicly-traded companies, from biopharmaceuticals to medical devices and healthcare services worldwide.

To thrive, organisms need to adapt and grow. So do investment firms. Through 25 years of volatile, changing investment environments, we've embraced new opportunities and expanded our global footprint.

about: At Playground our mission is simple: to move civilization forward through the power of technology.

When we started Playground, we weren’t just launching another venture firm—we were building the firm we wished we’d had when we were starting our own companies. We knew firsthand that the boldest ideas don’t just need capital; they need deep technical expertise, long-term vision, and a partner who understands the complexities of building from first principles.

With $1.7 billion in assets under management, we invest in early-stage deep tech startups tackling the world’s hardest problems—companies reinventing computing, AI, automation, materials, and more. Based in Palo Alto, we work side by side with founders, helping them turn ambitious ideas into world-changing businesses.
We don’t just bet on the future—we help build it.

We’ve built companies, pushed the limits of technology, and tackled the same challenges as the founders we back. This dual perspective gives us deep technical insight, real-world empathy, and an unshakable belief that today’s impossible ideas will define tomorrow’s world.

Innovation happens at the intersection of disciplines. We approach investing with a broad technical lens—where advances in one domain, like next-generation computing, can unlock breakthroughs in others, from engineered biology to energy transition.

We invest in technologies that matter—breakthroughs solving fundamental challenges, not just chasing trends. By prioritizing meaningful advancements over fleeting buzz, we identify transformative opportunities others overlook.
home: We invest somewhere between improbable and impossible. ‍
Playground is where the biggest leaps in engineering and science grow into companies of consequence. Wherever they start, we’re the bridge to where they’re going.

We’re entering the next great inflection point in compute. Playground backs the innovations pushing computing to new frontiers—from quantum computing and AI acceleration to novel architectures and advanced interconnects.
Automation isn’t the end goal—it’s a means to real outcomes. We invest in automation technologies that deliver tangible ROI by unlocking new ways for companies to scale, innovate, and compete.

The future of energy isn’t just cleaner—it’s smarter. Playground invests in technology that drives the energy transition—unlocking cleaner, more efficient, and scalable solutions across energy generation, storage, and infrastructure.
Biology is now programmable. At the intersection of AI and synthetic biology, Playground backs platforms that accelerate drug development and enable next-generation therapies.

Playground is where deep tech gets its start. We invest at the earliest stages of company formation, backing technical founders working at the intersection of AI, engineered biology, next-gen compute, and hard science. If it’s too early for everyone else, it’s probably right for us.

Playground companies don’t always fit into categories—they create them. From novel machines to programmable matter, our portfolio is proof that deep tech isn’t just a thesis—it’s a catalyst reshaping how the world works.

home: The founders and companies we're partnering with to change the world and shape a brighter future

Healthcare systems are under pressure. Chronic diseases are rising, populations are aging, and access to quality care still depends on income or geography, leaving too many people behind while costs continue to climb.

We believe AI diagnostics, digital therapeutics, provider software, and biotech innovation will redefine how people stay healthy. These technologies make prevention scalable, personalize care, and strengthen the connection between patients and providers. We back founders building solutions that detect earlier, treat smarter, and help people live not only longer lives, but better ones.

Financial systems remain fragmented and outdated. People still struggle to access fair credit, invest with confidence, or build long-term security through property ownership. Barriers, inefficiencies, and lack of trust continue to slow progress.

We believe AI agents, robotics, modern collaboration, and continuous learning will redefine how work gets done. about: Jacqueline is a seasoned entrepreneur , investor , and finance professional with nearly three decades of experience spanning private banking, asset management, and venture capital. After building a successful career in leading Swiss financial institutions, she founded her independent wealth management company in 2011, driven by the ambition to offer a more entrepreneurial and impact-oriented approach to investing.

Her passion for innovation and long-term value creation led her to enter venture capital in 2014, launching her first VC initiatives and later co-founding Privilège Ventures in 2021 . Under her leadership, the firm has become a recognized player in the Swiss and European venture ecosystem, investing in high-potential early-stage technology companies across sectors such as HealthTech, DeepTech, ClimateTech, AgrifoodTech, and AI.

Jacqueline is particularly committed to backing resilient and visionary entrepreneurs and has been a strong advocate for diverse leadership teams, recognizing their proven ability to generate stronger performance and long-term returns. She actively contributes to the startup ecosystem as a mentor, speaker, jury member, and board member for several innovative technology and MedTech companies.
Angelica is an experienced investor , entrepreneur , and strategic advisor with an international career spanning investment banking, asset management, venture capital, and innovation ecosystems.

She began her career in investment banking before founding her own asset management company in the United States in the late 1990s , driven by a strong entrepreneurial spirit and a vision for independent, forward-looking investment management. Over the years, she has built extensive expertise across asset allocation, portfolio construction, alternative investments, and private markets, advising both institutional and private investors across diverse geographies and market cycles.

She combines rigorous financial analysis with a strong ability to anticipate macroeconomic and technological trends , contributing to the firm's conviction-driven approach to venture capital investing. Beyond investing, Angelica is deeply engaged in entrepreneurship, education, and community building. She is an active speaker, mentor, and advocate for innovation, female leadership, and financial education, regularly contributing to initiatives that empower entrepreneurs and investors alike.

Nicole oversees business operations at Privilège Ventures, ensuring efficient coordination across internal processes , strategic initiatives, and community activities. With a strong organizational mindset and a proactive approach, she supports the firm's daily operations while fostering meaningful connections within the venture ecosystem.
Combining precision , adaptability , and energy , Nicole plays a key role in enhancing collaboration, streamlining workflows, and contributing to the dynamic growth of the firm and its network.

about: A European fund shaped by deep sector immersion and hands-on expertise. We think independently. We question assumptions. When conviction is there, we act, deliberately and without hesitation.
Anaïs is an Investment Associate at PT1, focusing on sourcing, evaluating, and supporting early-stage technology companies across the real asset value chain.

Prior to joining PT1, Anaïs worked as a Real Estate Investment Analyst at eRE – element Real Estate, where she gained hands-on experience in underwriting, financial modelling, and asset-level decision-making. Her work involved evaluating real estate investments from both a risk and return perspective, providing her with a strong foundation in assessing capital allocation decisions - skills directly transferable to venture investing.

Earlier in her career, Anaïs built a strong analytical toolkit as a Valuation & Risk Analyst at homeloop, where she focused on pricing models and risk assessment in a technology-driven real estate context. This role gave her early exposure to data-driven decision-making and scalable proptech business models, shaping her understanding of how technology can transform traditional asset classes.

She began her career in strategy and project roles at Publicis Luxe and OUTSIGN, developing a structured approach to problem-solving, market positioning, and stakeholder communication, skills that are critical in evaluating founding teams and supporting portfolio companies.

Anaïs holds a Master’s degree in Business Management from EDHEC Business School and a Master of Arts in International Business and Sustainability from the University of Hamburg, combining a strong business foundation with a focus on sustainable transformation.

As early as 1998, Anja joined her first startup immediately after finishing her A-Levels (Abitur), initially as an intern in the finance department. This startup was one of the first companies co-founded by Nikolas Samios in Munich. She quickly assumed more responsibility in the growing company and soon replaced the previous COO/CFO in all his duties.

Parallel to her work in financial management, organizational development, and general management, Anja studied part-time at the British OU University in Milton Keynes and received both a Master’s in International Finance and an MBA.

protego.vc.desc: We aim to propel forward exceptional companies that will help secure the safety and prosperity of the world and deliver out-sized returns for our investors.
home: Funding Next-Generation Defense Technologies
To support innovative companies and provide meaningful returns for our investors while contributing to advancements in defense and security in a rapidly changing world.

Protego Ventures is an Israel-based fund investing in early-growth companies driving innovation in critical areas of defense technology. The growing geopolitical instability, compounded by introduction of defense technology, has dramatically changed the defense landscape. There is an urgent need for cutting edge defense solutions. Israel, forced by necessity and driven by ingenuity, has been at the forefront meeting these needs. By rapidly innovating and building next-generation tools, Israel is proving their efficiency on the battlefield.
AI & Machine Learning Sensors Drones UAVs

As a pioneering fund in this sector, we invest in early growth-stage companies across key defense areas, including sensors, AI/ML, and autonomous systems such as drones and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).

XTEND provides human-guided autonomous machine systems that enable operators to perform extremely accurate makeovers and actions in any environment with minimal training. The company's patented XOS operating system fuses the best of human intelligence and machine autonomy to enhance the operator's abilities and reduce the need for physical confrontation, thereby minimizing casualties and injuries.
Unparalleled Access to Defense Priorities

Our exclusive partnerships and deep relationships across Israel, the United States, and allied nations position us at the forefront of defense priorities and innovation. These invaluable insights, coupled with our team’s expertise, enable high-conviction investment decisions that result in exceptional returns.

Our team of seasoned experts guides companies through critical growth stages all the way to successful exits. We navigate complex regulations, build high-performing teams, and leverage a vast partner network across the United States and allied nations to unlock opportunities and secure contracts.

Our deep ties across Israel’s dynamic defense ecosystem give us privileged access to the companies and cutting-edge innovations that are poised to revolutionize the defense landscape. By empowering innovators, we enhance Israel’s defense capabilities, secure a safer future, and deliver minimized risks with maximized financial returns for investors.

Shane is responsible for ProVen’s VCT fundraising and investor relations. Shane has over 16 years’ experience in raising equity for alternative investment funds.

psv.xyz.desc: PSV cares about a conscious future. As a venture house, our mission is to clear the path for founders who build companies that matter. Our hybrid setup, comprising PSV Foundry, PSV Lab, and two unique venture funds, PSV Tech and PSV Hafnium, sets us free from adhering to a singular method. Rather we rethink existing ways and models to maximise our impact beyond any individual firm or investment. Together, we can punch above our weight.
home: PSV is a venture house built to clear the path for founders who build companies that matter.
From taking the startup journey with 450+ founders, we know startup life way beyond metrics and facts.
We operated as a state-funded tech investor for two decades, willing to take bets on founders before anyone else. Over the years this has given us a front-row seat to the Danish startup ecosystem.

More than 75% of the companies in our portfolio have gone on to raise follow-on funding. Today we see almost every new startup emerging from Denmark. With visibility into 98% of the market, we get an early read on where the ecosystem is heading next.
This is the legacy we have leveraged to build a venture house with the vision to multiply our impact beyond any individual fund or investment.

Across PSV Foundry, PSV Tech and PSV Hafnium, we work as one extended team. Beyond capital, we contribute experience, operational support and long-term partnership, tailored to each founder’s journey.
Our approach is shaped by years of building, testing and refining what founders actually need when building companies from first proof to global scale.
This is where our shared capabilities live — from brand & communication to legal, finance, people & culture and ESG & impact integration.
Not as a fixed program or playbook, but as a flexible way of working that adapts to different stages, technologies and ambitions.
Dive deeper into the capabilities and initiatives that founders across PSV rely on.

home: We are an investment partner supporting you to make the world a better place.
Purpose Ventures is a venture capital fund based in Perth, Western Australia. We back founders who are chasing after their life cause, and we partner with you to help you get there.

Our team have been founders themselves, so we know what this crazy journey can be like. We've been investing in and supporting companies for over a decade and founders choose to work with us because of our highly relational approach. Simply put... we care.
We are industry agnostic and invest from Pre-Seed to Series B rounds. We are looking for purpose-driven founders, who have ambition to build companies that can have global impact.

We have a long, successful track record of establishing, scaling and exiting a number of companies. We use that experience to help you build an awesome company. Here's our team and you can read more about How We Help .
There's lots we look for in the detail (you can find more at our Investment FAQs and Investment Process ), but at a high level these are the first things we're thinking about when we get to meet you.
If you're chasing your life cause and you've got the ambition to get there then we look for:
Character - so we can trust what you do and say.
Competency - knowing you are good at what you do.
Chemistry - checking the vibes when we're together.

about: RAISE, groupe européen d’investissement, pionnier de la finance engagée
Nous affirmons un positionnement pionnier, source d'une croissance durable

Convaincus que la finance est l’un des leviers les plus puissants de transformation de notre économie et qu’elle peut impulser un changement systémique positif, Clara Gaymard et Gonzague de Blignières ont créé RAISE : un groupe d'investissement pionnier en Europe, qui concilie performance et générosité, croissance et durabilité, finance et bien commun. ‍
Naissance de RAISE, groupe pionnier d’une finance engagée et responsable et création de notre première activité : RAISE Invest .
Le Groupe signe les Principles for Responsable Investment et crée le fonds de dotation RAISE Sherpas , financé par la générosité des équipes d’investissement.

Avec l’aide de l’ensemble de ses collaborateurs, RAISE formalise sa première Raison d'Être : “Soutenir des entrepreneurs passionnés et visionnaires pour les aider à concrétiser leurs rêves et leurs projets.” Le Groupe lance deux nouvelles activités, RAISE REIM et RAISE Ventures.

Avec la création de RAISE Impact , le Groupe prend une nouvelle impulsion, encore plus engagée pour la transformation de notre économie. Les équipes développent une Méthodologie de Mesure et de Management de l’Impact propriétaire. Le Groupe structure sa politique ESG, étendue à l’ensemble de ses activités. RAISE Sherpas , en collaboration avec le Crédit Agricole d’Ile-de-France, lance le prêt RAISE Expansion.

RAISE Impact signe les Operating Principles for Impact Management de l’IFC. Durant la crise de la Covid-19, l’ensemble du Groupe se mobilise pour accompagner ses participations et plus largement les startups au travers de RAISE Sherpas . Avec l’aide du Laboratoire des Mines ParisTech, de MySezame et de l’ensemble des collaborateurs, le Groupe met à jour sa Raison d’Être.

RET Ventures Blueprint Main Event Recap Blog

At this year’s Blueprint conference, RET Ventures’ Multifamily & SFR Summit explored how owners and operators can turn technology into measurable operational value. Two additional sessions during the main Blueprint program extended that conversation, examining a related challenge: as technology becomes more accessible, how can operators use it to create a lasting competitive advantage?

The breakout session, “If AI Commoditizes Leasing, What Makes You Different?” explored what this challenge looks like as AI transforms the renter journey. Moderated by RET Principal Aaron Ru, the panel featured Garrett Hrncir of Continental Properties, Kim Garfield of UDR and Tyler Christiansen of Funnel. The discussion centered on a growing possibility: as operators adopt similar AI tools for prospect engagement, property discovery and virtual tours, technology itself may become less of a differentiator.

Instead, operators will need to be more intentional about where automation adds value and where human interaction will do more to change the outcome. AI can make leasing faster and more accessible, but personal attention still matters when prospective residents have specific concerns, need help navigating a decision or are considering whether to renew. The opportunity is to use technology to streamline routine tasks while allowing employees to focus on the interactions that build trust and strengthen the resident experience.

about: From getting America online to backing a new era of innovation and community, we invest in what's next—and where it's happening.

When I launched AOL more than three decades ago, the idea that people could use technology to connect and build community—regardless of where they lived—felt like a radical bet. But it was a bet on the future, and what I called the killer app: people. At its peak, half of all U.S. internet traffic ran through AOL, and more than half of that usage was via community-related features: email, message boards, chat rooms, and instant messaging (AIM name: Steve—it pays to get in early).
That same belief in the power of community drives everything we do at Revolution.

We started this firm with a simple conviction: innovation isn’t confined to pre-selected pins on a map. Great companies—and great communities—can rise up anywhere. That idea has guided our approach to venture investing, real estate development, and hospitality.
Whether we’re backing a startup rethinking logistics in the Midwest or developing a resort that redefines cultural immersion in Costa Rica, we go where the potential is and help unlock it.

To us, place matters, not just as geography, but as context. We don’t believe in parachuting in. We’ve seen what happens when investors take the long-term view and engage deeply in the places where they invest. That’s why we back startups not just with capital, but with connections, and a commitment to helping them thrive where they are. And it’s why we build properties that strengthen communities—housing to support growing workforces, and destinations that promote wellbeing and reflect the spirit of their surroundings.

We believe in showing up, listening closely, and partnering with people on the ground to create something that lasts, whether that’s a business, a travel destination, or a broader movement. And because of our D.C. homebase, we also relentlessly champion policies that support those efforts.
This isn’t just about investing. It’s about building. And it’s about shaping an economy where more people in more places have the chance to thrive.

about: Odense Robotics StartUp Fund is a new, non-profit model for shaping successful robotic startups for generations to come. The independent commercial foundation offers early-stage robotic and drone startups from Denmark and abroad access to founder-friendly investment, cutting-edge know-how from leading robotic business leaders and world-class incubator facilities at the Danish Technological Institute in Odense.

The fund invests directly in startups. Returns from loans and additional payments made in the event of acquisitions are reinvested in the fund and in turn in new startups. This long-term, sustainable model aims to create a continuous flow of strong robotic and drone startups – bringing lasting benefits to startup founders, investors, Denmark’s robotics industry and the surrounding community.

Startups also gain unique access to cutting-edge robotic know-how from a group of experts. Some of the Fund’s founders – which includes prominent robotic businesspeople – act as mentors for startups, offering trusted advice based on their deep sector knowledge and extensive industry experience. In addition, technical experts from the Danish Technological Institute advise startups on tech development, while coaches from Odense Robotics advise startups on business development.

Odense Robotics StartUp Fund has a total capital of DKK 18.4M consisting of donations from key figures from some of Denmark’s most successful robot companies, influential robot investors and prominent commercial foundations behind some of the country’s largest industrial companies.

sallinggroup.com.desc: Salling Group er Danmarks største dagligvarekoncern med kæder som føtex, Bilka, Netto, Salling stormagasiner, BR og butikker i Danmark, Tyskland og Polen.
home: Se ledige stillinger Se video Salling – flere muligheder

I vores nye brandkampagne kan du møde nogle af de kollegaer, der hver dag er med til at gøre Salling Group til mere end bare en arbejdsplads. Hør deres historier, oplev kulturen indefra, og få en fornemmelse af, hvordan det er at være en del af et fællesskab, hvor vi sammen løfter i flok.

Salling Group er Danmarks største dagligvarekoncern med kæder som føtex, Bilka, Netto, Salling stormagasiner og BR i Danmark. Salling Group ejer og driver desuden Netto-butikker i Tyskland og Polen og Rimi-butikker i Estland, Letland og Litauen.

Vores valg gør en forskel for både kunder, kolleger, samarbejdspartnere, leverandører og det samfund, vi er en del af. Derfor har vi et stort ansvar, og det tager vi på os, når vi hver eneste dag arbejder for at gøre hverdagen bedre.

Fordi vi er 100 % ejet af Salling Fondene, går en del af vores overskud tilbage til samfundet. Siden 2012 har Salling Fondene doneret 2,5 milliarder kroner til uddannelse, kultur, sport, socialt arbejde og andre gode formål.
Lige siden Ferdinand Salling åbnede den første Salling butik på Søndergade 34 i Aarhus, har Salling Group handlet om at forbedre hverdagen. Og morgendagen.

Forandringer og udfordringer i verden påvirker vores kunders hverdag og adfærd. Hverken politikere, virksomheder eller forbrugere kan løse disse udfordringer alene. Det er et fælles ansvar, som vi er en del af.

Som Danmarks største dagligvarekoncern vil vi hjælpe vores kunder til at kunne handle mere ansvarligt og klimabevidst i hverdagen. I Salling Group har vi derfor altid arbejdet med ansvarlighed, og vores arbejde hviler på hele fundamentet for vores virksomhed; nemlig kunder, medarbejdere og de varer, vi sælger.

I 2024 indgik Salling Group og DBU en historisk aftale om at sætte ligeværd, bedre trivsel og uddannelse på banen. Partnerskabet omfatter som det første af sin slags alle landshold fra U16 og op til Kvinde- og Herrelandsholdet, Pigeraketten og DBU Fodboldskole.

Rimi Baltic er en af Baltikums største dagligvarekoncerner med hovedkontor i Riga. Salling Group overtog Rimi Baltic i 2025, og virksomheden driver i dag 314 butikker fordelt på fire kæder: Rimi Hypermarkets, Rimi Super, Rimi Mini og Rimi Express. Virksomheden beskæftiger over 11.000 medarbejdere og opererer med lagre og distributionscentre på tværs af alle tre baltiske lande.

about: Our story started in 2015, with Deep Tech founders who couldn’t find the resources they needed to build their ventures, so decided to take matters into their own hands.

Since then, we have worked to develop a UK-wide platform of support where Deep Tech startups can thrive. With technical founders and their teams always at the heart, the Science Creates ecosystem includes five pillars of activity that target key aspects of a startup’s journey — from ideation to growth — while also bringing science closer to people of all ages to inspire them to engage with STEM and entrepreneurship.

The story of Science Creates traces its roots back to 2014, with Ziylo, a University of Bristol spinout that developed a breakthrough platform technology for diabetes treatment. When Ziylo tried to find lab space in the city to continue developing its tech, the team found that none existed outside of the Golden Triangle.

Ziylo Co-Founder Harry Destecroix figured his couldn’t be the only technical team facing this barrier, so he started to rally people and resources to build Bristol’s first Deep Tech incubator. Science Creates was born, and its first incubator opened its doors in 2017.
A year after moving into the new incubator, Ziylo exited in a deal worth up to $800m.

Since then, Science Creates has significantly grown in size and scope but the core principle that started it all remains: supporting technical founders to take their scientific discoveries off the bench and change the world through advanced technologies for people, planet, and long-term economic renewal.

Our activities now span five pillars of support for the Deep Tech community: Incubators (specialised lab space and services), VC (investment), Platform (training, events and partnerships), Development (end-to-end design for lab and R&D facilities) and Outreach (STEM programmes and public engagement).
Our pillars work together to empower those who are reshaping the world through science now, and those who will in generations to come.

home: We invest in Pre-seed and Seed companies. Our model enables us to flex up or down, but our initial check is typically 750k-$1.5M. We structured our fund to give founders the best advantage at the most critical early stage, meaning: we right-size checks to what your company needs. The result is less dilution for you and greater latitude to bring the best partners into your round, while focusing our time on your company growth.

We typically make investment decisions within 1-2 weeks, following the first meeting. We meet once over Zoom or in person with prospective founders, and then bring in the rest of the team for a couple more meetings. We don't require consensus, but all of us have to be excited about every investment.

We're focused on AI native companies. We look at the founders, the opportunity they're going after, and how they think. We ask ourselves: What about this person and their history demonstrates they can do things that are extremely unlikely? In what ways are they reinventing an existing market, or creating a totally new one? And what is it about these individuals that give them an innate edge?

We focus on product and go-to-market because that's where our team has a lot of experience. Right after the investment, we set-up a WhatsApp thread with each founding team so we can jump in on any big challenges or critical milestones. That often leads to calls or in-person sessions, plus introductions to key people in our circle. We are highly responsive, and we take our role with each company seriously.
We poll our founders regularly for feedback, here's what they say .

We're a crew of product and go-to-market leaders from OpenAI, Meta, Twitter, and a16z. We exist to back the world's best AI native founders and help them reshape our world for the better. We go wide on product and deep on GTM. We are most often the first backer, and we invest selectively so we can give our maximum time and effort at the critical early stages.
We surround ourselves with some of the greatest minds in technology.
Our founders aren't a portfolio - they're our people.

about: Bill Maris is an entrepreneur, venture capitalist, and technology executive. He is the founder of S32, a venture capital firm investing at the frontiers of innovation. His investment track record includes iconic, category-defining companies such as Uber, Nest, Slack, CrowdStrike, Coinbase, and Flatiron Health - that have collectively grown to hundreds of billions of dollars in market value, generating billions of dollars of returns.

Bill is the founder and former CEO of Google Ventures (GV), the venture capital arm of Alphabet, Inc., and previously served as Alphabet’s Vice President of Special Projects. Working closely with Google’s founders, he helped incubate and launch major initiatives including Google X, Waymo, and Verily, while leading global investment activities for Alphabet. His leadership spanned a broad array of cutting-edge technologies—from cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure to aviation, artificial intelligence and robotics.

During his tenure at Google, Bill founded Calico, a multi-billion-dollar company focused on understanding the biology of aging and lifespan. He served on the board of Nest and recruited the CEOs of Verily, Chronicle, and Calico. Earlier in his career, Bill founded one of the world’s first web-hosting companies and worked at Sweden-based Investor AB. He also assisted MacArthur Fellow David Green in transferring a hydrophobic acrylic lens technology to Aurolab, where it has since helped prevent or cure cataract blindness in millions of underserved people worldwide.
Andy currently serves as the CEO and General Partner of S32, drawing on a distinguished career in leadership roles at Alphabet’s most innovative divisions.

During his tenure at GoogleX, he worked on a diverse portfolio of projects involving AI, robotics, cybersecurity, and quantum computing. His strategic guidance was central to the successful spin-out of SandboxAQ and Intrinsic (acquired by Google). He remains an active advisor to GoogleX.

At Google Life Sciences (Verily), Andy was a member of the executive leadership team as the Global Head of Business and Corporate Development. In this capacity, he pioneered go-to-market campaigns, partnerships and joint ventures with world leading healthcare companies. These efforts fueled Verily’s rapid expansion and multi-billion dollar financings. He also co-founded Verily Ventures, which delivered top-tier returns, and was a founding member of Granular Insurance, a reinsurance subsidiary recently acquired by Elevance.

Before his time at Google, Andy’s entrepreneurial track record included building a Stanford-seeded startup that was successfully acquired and a second company that continues to grow and scale. He began his career within the DFJ Global Venture Network.

Today, he is a widely recognized authority in artificial intelligence, frequently speaking at prestigious universities and major industry conferences. His insights are often featured in leading publications such as The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, Forbes, and Fortune.
